examples.english: John Nash, who received a Nobel Prize in economics, thought that when it came to math, nobody was better than he was.
examples.japanese: 経済学のノーベル賞を受賞したジョン・ナシュは数学にかけては自分の右に出る者はいないと思っていた。

examples.english: Jackie Chan is an actor with whom none can compete when it comes to action ﬁlms.
examples.japanese: ジャッキー・チェンは、アクションにかけては右に出る者がいない俳優である。

examples.english: For policy making in this ﬁeld, Mr. Yamazaki has the best insight and experience in the political world.
examples.japanese: 山崎氏はこの分野の政策立案にかけては政界随一の見識と経験を持っている。

examples.english: Photography overwhelmingly surpasses paintings in terms of objective reproduction.
examples.japanese: 写真というものは絵画に比べて、その客観的再現力にかけては圧倒的にまさっている。

examples.english: One of the special features of this youth hostel is that people of any age can stay here (literally: use it), and when it comes to comfort, it is among the top-rated (hostels) in the world.
examples.japanese: このユースホステルは年齢を問わず誰でも利用でき、快適さにかけては世界中でも最高クラスだ。

examples.english: When it comes to the production of special steels, this factory has the world's best technology.
examples.japanese: この工場は特殊鋼の製造にかけては世界屈指の技術を有している。

points.explanation: A compound particle that marks something in which someone excels or has conﬁdence.
points.meaning: When it comes to ~; as for; in point of; in terms of; about; regarding

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | にかけては | |
| 音楽にかけては | When it comes to music |

examples.english: It is not hard to imagine that the quality of teachers fell because of the low salary.
examples.japanese: 給料が低いために教師の質が低下した（であろう）ことは想像にかたくない。

examples.english: It is easy to guess how miserable her life was after she lost her parents.
examples.japanese: 幼い時に両親を失った彼女の生活が｛いかに/どれほど｝悲惨だったかは推測にかたくない。

examples.english: It is easy to imagine them spending a lot of money on this new house.
examples.japanese: この新宅には相当お金をかけたであろうことは想像にかたくない。

examples.english: It is not hard to imagine that behind the eye-opening progress Japanese language education has made are the extraordinary efforts of Japanese language educators and researchers.
examples.japanese: 日本語教育のめざましい進歩の裏には、日本語教育者・研究者の並々ならぬ努力があったことは、想像にかたくありません。

examples.english: It isn't hard to imagine how difﬁcult it has become for foreign students to ﬁnd (examples of) traditional Japanese culture.
examples.japanese: 留学生にとって日本の伝統文化を見つけることがいかに難しくなっているかは想像にかたくないことでしょう。

examples.english: It isn't hard to imagine that a man of his versatile talents struggled (to choose) between his beloved world of literature and his managerial responsibilities.
examples.japanese: 好きな文芸の道と経営者としての責任の間で、多才な彼が苦悩していたことは想像にかたくない。

examples.english: It is easy to imagine that young man as a gentle, serious and diligent person.
examples.japanese: その青年が非常に心優しく生真面目かつ勉学熱心な人間だったことは推測にかたくない。

examples.english: It isn't hard to predict that if people who live overseas and actively criticize the military regime of their country go home, most likely they will be put into prison and tortured.
examples.japanese: 海外に在住して母国の軍事政権への反対活動を行っている人が帰国すれば、拘禁や拷問にさらされるであろうことは予測にかたくない。

points.explanation: にかたくない・に難くない A phrase that indicates that it is not hard to imagine or guess a situation.
points.meaning: Not hard; easy ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
VN | に難くない | Where VN=Sino-Japanese compound |
| {想像/推測/予測}に難くない | It is not hard to imagine/guess/predict |

examples.english: It is a given that a good personality is preferable.
examples.japanese: 性格は、いい方がいいに決まっている。

examples.english: Of course customers want to buy things cheaply.
examples.japanese: お客さまだって安く買いたいに決まっているじゃないか。

examples.english: To keep writing nothing but Chinese characters is bound to be boring.
examples.japanese: ただただ漢字を書くなんて、つまらないに決まっている。

examples.english: If you're just going on an errand to the tobacco shop around the comer, it's more convenient to go there by bike than by car — no question about it!
examples.japanese: すぐ角のタバコ屋に行く程度の用事なら、車より自転車の方が便利に決まっている。

examples.english: When I closely observe the magniﬁcent X chromosome and the small Y chromosome, it seems like women are bound to be healthier.
examples.japanese: 立派なX染色体と小さなY染色体をつくづく見ていると、女性の方が丈夫に決まっていると思う。

examples.english: If the merchandise is the same, people will always buy at a store with a good atmosphere.
examples.japanese: 同じ商品なら気持ちのいい店で買うに決まっている。

examples.english: Children grow up in a society that adults create. So, if the children are not normal, it is a given that the adults are at fault.
examples.japanese: 子供は、大人が作っている社会の中で育つのだから、子供が変なのは大人のせいに決まっている。

examples.english: (Are you asking me) what I came here for? Of course I came here to drink!
examples.japanese: 何しに来たって？飲みに来たに決まっているじゃないか。

points.explanation: A phrase indicating the speaker’s/writer’s strong conviction or motivation.
points.meaning: Surely; be bound to; be a given; of course; must be; we all know that

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | に決まっている | |
| {来る/来た}に決まっている | Someone is bound to show up/someone must have come |
| {高い/高かった}に決まっている | Something must be/have been expensive |
(ii) {Adjectiveなstem/ Noun} | {∅/だった}に決まっている | |
| 上手{∅/だった}に決まっている | Someone is/was surely good at it |
| 日本人{∅/だった}に決まっている | Someone must be/have been Japanese |

examples.english: The more buddies you have the better.
examples.japanese: 仲間は多いに越したことはない。

examples.english: The healthier the better.
examples.japanese: 元気（である）に越したことはない。

examples.english: For cavities, nothing is better than prevention.
examples.japanese: 虫歯は予防する（の）に越したことはない。

examples.english: A constant temperature is ideal.
examples.japanese: 温度は一定（である）に越したことはない。

examples.english: A good environment is the best.
examples.japanese: 環境はよいに越したことはない。

examples.english: Regarding working hours, the shorter the better, right?
examples.japanese: 働く時間は短いに越したことはないんじゃないの？

examples.english: A clean room is best.
examples.japanese: 部屋は清潔に越したことはない。

examples.english: My son is mischievous beyond our control, but nothing is more important than his being healthy.
examples.japanese: うちの息子はわんぱくで手に余る。まあ、元気に越したことはないけれど。

examples.english: I will be on summer vacation for ﬁve days from this Saturday through next Wednesday. I don't have any particular plan, but having days off is better than work.
examples.japanese: 今週の土曜日から来週水曜日までの5日間、僕も夏休みに入ります。特別な予定もないけど仕事より休みに越したことはありません。

examples.english: We should avoid pain, and having none is best.
examples.japanese: 痛みは避けるべきものであり、ないに越したことはない。

examples.english: There would be nothing better than being able to say on Christmas Day, "You're the best gift I could have."
examples.japanese: クリスマスに「私にとって最高の贈り物はあなたです」なんて言葉が言えるに越したことはない。

examples.english: No matter how well-developed networks are, when it comes to real communication, nothing is better than talking face to face.
examples.japanese: ネットワークがどれだけ発達しても、本当のコミュニケーションには、人と人とが向かい合って話すのに越したことはない。

points.explanation: A phrase used to indicate that a state or action is more desirable.
points.meaning: Nothing is better than; if possible; be the best; be ideal; the ~ the ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Adjectiveいinformal nonpast | に越したことはない | |
| 安いに越したことはない | The cheaper the better |
(ii) {Adjectiveなstem/Noun} | (である) に越したことはない | |
| 静か(である) に越したことはない | The quieter the better |
| 英語(である) に越したことはない | English is the best |
(iii) Vinformal nonpast | (の) に越したことはない | |
| 我慢する(の) に越したことはない | Patience is the best |

examples.english: In the cherry blossom season (literally: When it becomes the cherry blossom season), this park is packed with cherry blossom viewers.
examples.japanese: 桜の季節｛に/と｝もなるとこの公園は花見客でにぎわう。

examples.english: When you go abroad, most likely you will want to study that country's language and culture.
examples.japanese: 外国へ行くともなると、その国の言語や文化を勉強したくなるはずだ。

examples.english: On New Year's Day my friends and I go to each other's houses and enjoy New Year's Day sake.
examples.japanese: 正月ともなると、友人同士、お互いの家を行き来して、正月酒を楽しむ。

examples.english: When the leaves begin turning red, the number of visitors starts to increase, and in mid-November, this place is packed with people.
examples.japanese: ここは紅葉が始まると訪れる人が増え始め、11月半ばともなると大勢の人でごったがえす。

examples.english: Once you (graduate and) get out in the real world, you will start getting invited to the weddings of your elders and friends.
examples.japanese: 社会人にもなると、先輩や友人の結婚式に招かれる機会が出てきます。

examples.english: When you become a high school student, you get a part-time job and start earning your own pocket money.
examples.japanese: 高校生にもなると、自分のお小遣いくらいは、バイトして稼ぐようになる。

examples.english: At a big hotel, thousands of people come through daily.
examples.japanese: 大きなホテルともなると、一日に数千人もの利用者が集まってくる。

examples.english: "Beauty and the Beast" is a popular show, so it's hard to ﬁnd same day tickets.
examples.japanese: 『美人と野獣』ともなると人気の作品だから、当日券なんてなかなか買えない。

examples.english: When you enter college, each of you will develop your own lifestyle, with studies, work and club activities.
examples.japanese: 大学へ進学するともなると、学問、バイト、サークルなど、人それぞれのライフスタイルができてくる。

examples.english: Starting this year, we're going to Hokkaido for our school trip, and the thought of ﬂying there has made us so excited we can hardly stand it.
examples.japanese: 今年から修学旅行先が北海道になり、飛行機で行くともなると、胸を躍らさずにはいられなかった。

points.explanation: に/ともなると A phrase that is used when something or some situation is perceived to be special.
points.meaning: When; if; as

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | {に/と}もなると | |
| 五月{に/と}もなると | Literally: when it becomes May; in May |
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | ともなると | |
| 退職するともなると | When someone retires |

examples.english: In the cherry blossom season (literally: When it becomes the cherry blossom season), this park is packed with cherry blossom viewers.
examples.japanese: 桜の季節｛に/と｝もなるとこの公園は花見客でにぎわう。

examples.english: When you go abroad, most likely you will want to study that country's language and culture.
examples.japanese: 外国へ行くともなると、その国の言語や文化を勉強したくなるはずだ。

examples.english: On New Year's Day my friends and I go to each other's houses and enjoy New Year's Day sake.
examples.japanese: 正月ともなると、友人同士、お互いの家を行き来して、正月酒を楽しむ。

examples.english: When the leaves begin turning red, the number of visitors starts to increase, and in mid-November, this place is packed with people.
examples.japanese: ここは紅葉が始まると訪れる人が増え始め、11月半ばともなると大勢の人でごったがえす。

examples.english: Once you (graduate and) get out in the real world, you will start getting invited to the weddings of your elders and friends.
examples.japanese: 社会人にもなると、先輩や友人の結婚式に招かれる機会が出てきます。

examples.english: When you become a high school student, you get a part-time job and start earning your own pocket money.
examples.japanese: 高校生にもなると、自分のお小遣いくらいは、バイトして稼ぐようになる。

examples.english: At a big hotel, thousands of people come through daily.
examples.japanese: 大きなホテルともなると、一日に数千人もの利用者が集まってくる。

examples.english: "Beauty and the Beast" is a popular show, so it's hard to ﬁnd same day tickets.
examples.japanese: 『美人と野獣』ともなると人気の作品だから、当日券なんてなかなか買えない。

examples.english: When you enter college, each of you will develop your own lifestyle, with studies, work and club activities.
examples.japanese: 大学へ進学するともなると、学問、バイト、サークルなど、人それぞれのライフスタイルができてくる。

examples.english: Starting this year, we're going to Hokkaido for our school trip, and the thought of ﬂying there has made us so excited we can hardly stand it.
examples.japanese: 今年から修学旅行先が北海道になり、飛行機で行くともなると、胸を躍らさずにはいられなかった。

points.explanation: に/ともなると A phrase that is used when something or some situation is perceived to be special.
points.meaning: When; if; as

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | {に/と}もなると | |
| 五月{に/と}もなると | Literally: when it becomes May; in May |
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | ともなると | |
| 退職するともなると | When someone retires |

points.explanation: に（も）なく A phrase that means something unusual happens or someone does something unusual.
points.meaning:
Unusually; more ~ than usual
-------------
〖example〗: (ks).
彼女は今日はいつに（も）なく陽気だった。
She was unusually cheerful today.

[例文B] (a). 宏は「ただいまー」といつになく明るい声で帰ってきた。
Hiroshi came home and said "I'm home!" in an unusually cheerful voice.

(b). 普段はたいていビールや日本酒だが、たまに柄にもなくバーにカクテルを飲みに行ったりする
Usually I drink beer or sake, but occasionally I may go out for cocktails at a bar, which is unlike me.

examples.english: The team of reporters left for the next destination.
examples.japanese: 報道班は次の目的地に向けて出発した。

examples.english: This TV commercial is being marketed to single women in their twenties and thirties.
examples.japanese: このテレビコマーシャルは20、30代の独身女性に向けて発信されている。

examples.english: I'm studying hard now for the next year's entrance exam.
examples.japanese: 今、来年の入学試験に向けて頑張っています。

examples.english: Research is progressing toward (the goal of) developing new energy.
examples.japanese: 新しいエネルギーの開発に向けて研究が進んでいる。

examples.english: Efforts to prevent (literally: Movement for the purpose of preventing) global warming are gaining vigour.
examples.japanese: 地球温暖化防止に｛向けての/向けた｝動きが活発化している。

examples.english: A helicopter loaded with relief supplies left for (literally: took off toward) the site of the damage.
examples.japanese: 救援物資を積んだヘリコプターが被災地に向けて飛び立った。

examples.english: The riot police shot tear gas bombs at the ranks of demonstrators.
examples.japanese: 機動隊はデモ隊に向けて催涙弾を発射した。

examples.english: Starting in January, K Company is going to export luxury cars to China which were manufactured in Kyushu.
examples.japanese: K社は1月から九州で生産した高級車を中国に向けて輸出する。

examples.english: In this project, animators from around the globe create works for the world's children, and then the works are translated into various countries' languages.
examples.japanese: このプロジェクトでは、世界各国のアニメーターが世界中の子供たちに向けて作品を作り、それをそれぞれの国の言葉に翻訳します。

examples.english: The volleyball association is hurrying to strengthen its players for the next Olympic Games.
examples.japanese: バレーボール協会は次のオリンピックに向けて選手の強化を急いでいる。

examples.english: Negotiations toward the global integration of incompatible (literally: different) patent systems began.
examples.japanese: 異なる特許制度の世界的統一に向けて交渉が開始された。

examples.english: H Company has established a new company for the commercialization of their newly-developed battery.
examples.japanese: H社は新しく開発された電池の事業化に向けて新会社を設立した。

examples.english: Our company is implementing a new communication system for more efﬁcient internal communication.
examples.japanese: 我が社は効率的な社内コミュニケーションに向けての新しいコミュニケーションシステムの導入を進めている。

examples.english: Mr. M's proposal was full of suggestions when we began considering the guiding principles of Japan's diplomacy for the new century.
examples.japanese: M氏の提言は、新たな世紀に向けた日本外交の指針を考えていくにあたり、非常に示唆に富むものであった。

points.meaning: Toward; to; at; aiming at; targeting; for; for the purpose of; in order to

(ii) VN | に向けて | |

(iii) Noun1 | に{向けての/向けた}Noun2 | |
| ２１世紀に{向けての/向けた}社会保障 | Social security for the 21st century |

examples.english: In response to union demands, the standard work day (literally: standard work hours) will be shortened.
examples.japanese: 組合の要求に応じて標準就業時間が短縮されることになった。

examples.english: Bonuses were distributed to all employees according to their performance (literally: achievements).
examples.japanese: 業績に応じて従業員全員にボーナスが支給された。

examples.english: Please make sure your driving is appropriate for the weather and road conditions.
examples.japanese: 天候や道路状況に応じた適切な運転を心がけましょう。

examples.english: We can also dispatch a lecturer to the school in response to their request.
examples.japanese: 当社では要請に応じて講師を学校に派遣することもできます。

examples.english: The drugs a patient receives at the hospital are prescribed by the doctor according to the patient's physical condition and symptoms.
examples.japanese: 病院でもらう薬は、医師が患者の体質や症状に応じて処方します。

examples.english: A wise way of using a water heater is to adjust the (pre-set) temperature each time, according to the purpose.
examples.japanese: 湯沸かし器の設定温度は、目的に応じてその都度調節するのが賢い使い方だ。

examples.english: According to the ""Survey of How Future Higher Education Should Be,"" which was conducted this year, 33.7 percent (of respondents) agreed that for effective foreign language education, ""classes should be taught by dividing students according to their ability"".
examples.japanese: 今年行われた「今後の大学教育のあり方に関する世論調査」によると、外国語教育の効果的だと思われる授業のあり方に関して、33.7％が「学生個人の能力に応じてクラスを分けて授業を行う」と答えた。

examples.english: Shampoo, which is indispensable for hair care, comes in various types, depending on the condition of your hair.
examples.japanese: 髪のケアには欠かせないシャンプーには症状に応じて様々なタイプがある。

examples.english: Generally, supply changes according to the demand. However, it is also true that in some cases demand changes according to the supply.
examples.japanese: 一般に供給は需要に応じて変動する。しかし、場合によって需要が供給に応じて変動するのも事実である。

examples.english: When buying a house, you should choose one that is within your means (literally: suitable for your income).
examples.japanese: 家を購入する場合には収入に応じた物件を選ぶべきです。

examples.english: We support the production of highly cost-effective Web pages geared to the customer's budget (literally: suitable for the customer's budget).
examples.japanese: 我が社はお客さまのご予算に応じた費用対効果の高いホームページ制作を支援します。

examples.english: The Law Regarding the Protection of Personal Information, which was promulgated in the ﬁfteenth year of Heisei (2003), requires businesses that handle personal information to disclose or correct an individual's personal data in their possession in response to the individual's demand, or to stop using the data in response to his/her demand.
examples.japanese: 平成15年に公布された「個人情報の保護に関する法律」は、個人情報取扱事業者に対し、本人の求めに応じて保有個人データの開示や訂正を行うこと、また本人の求めに応じてその利用を停止することなだを義務づけている。

points.meaning: In response to; according to; depending on; appropriate for; suitable for; suited to; meet

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

| 能力に応じて | According to someone’s ability |

| 目的に応じた教え方 | A teaching method suitable for the purpose |

examples.english: Even though he didn't have much time, this work is too sloppy.
examples.japanese: 時間があまりなかったに｛しろ/せよ｝、この仕事はひどすぎる。

examples.english: No matter who writes it, there can be absolutely no mistakes.
examples.japanese: 誰が書くに｛しろ/せよ｝、絶対間違いがあってはいけない。

examples.english: Whether you go or not, please give me a call later.
examples.japanese: 行くに｛しろ/せよ｝、行かないに｛しろ/せよ｝、後で電話を下さい。

examples.english: At any rate (literally: whatever it is), leaving the situation as it is won't solve the problem.
examples.japanese: 何に｛しろ/せよ｝、このままでは問題は解決しない。

examples.english: Even though it is just practice, you have to take it seriously.
examples.japanese: たとえ練習に｛しろ/せよ｝、真面目にやらなければならない。

examples.english: Although the degree may differ from country to country (literally: there may be differences in degree), there is no country without gender discrimination.
examples.japanese: 程度の差はあるにせよ、性差別のない国はないだろう。

examples.english: Even if (it's true that) taking the drug will not solve all your problems, in your case, you have to alleviate the symptoms ﬁrst (by taking it).
examples.japanese: 薬を飲むことですべての問題が解決はしないにしろ、あなたの場合は薬で症状を軽減させることが先決です。

examples.english: Even if we ask someone to write it for us, we will have to think of what to say (literally: the content) ourselves.
examples.japanese: 誰かに書いてもらうにしろ、内容は我々が考えなければならない。

examples.english: Whichever software application you use, you must quickly get comfortable using it (literally: get used to how to use it).
examples.japanese: どのソフトを使うにしろ、早く使い方に慣れてもらわないといけない。

examples.english: Whoever explains it (to him) must be very careful not to hurt his feelings.
examples.japanese: 誰がそれを説明するにせよ、相手の気持ちを傷つけないように細心の注意が必要だ。

examples.english: No matter what the circumstances were, quitting the job without saying anything is just (too) irresponsible.
examples.japanese: どんな事情があったにせよ、何も言わずに仕事を辞めるのは無責任すぎる。

examples.english: Books on Web page design are spilling off of bookstore shelves, and whether we want to read them ourselves or recommend them to someone else, it is hard to know what to choose.
examples.japanese: ホームページの制作に関する書籍は書店の棚にあふれている状態で、自分が読むにせよ、他人に勧めるにせよ、大いに迷う。

examples.english: First of all, whether you support the current administration or criticize it, an accurate understanding and a cool analysis of the problems are indispensable.
examples.japanese: 現政権を支持するにせよ批判するにせよ、まずはじめに問題に対する正確な理解と冷静な分析が不可欠である。

examples.english: Whether it be baseball or soccer, you cannot stay as a professional player just with an ordinary effort.
examples.japanese: 野球にせよサッカーにせよ、プロでやっていくには並の努力では続かない。

examples.english: Whether they do it consciously or unconsciously, ordinary people try to avoid unpleasant things.
examples.japanese: 普通の人は、意識的にせよ無意識的にせよ、不快なことを避けようとする。

examples.english: Whether it is true or not, once you send out information on the Internet, you can't take it back.
examples.japanese: 一旦ネットに発信してしまった情報は、それが真実にせよそうでないにせよ、取り消しができない。

points.explanation: にしろ・せよ A conjunctive phrase that carries the meaning of concession.
points.meaning: Even though (it is/was the case that); even if (it is true that); although (it is/was the case that); whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.; whether X or Y

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Vinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| {行く/行った}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though someone goes/went |
(ii) Adjectiveいinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| {高い/高かった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was expensive |
(iii) Adjectiveなstem | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | |
| 不十分{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was insufficient |
(iv) Noun | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | |
| 子供{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though it is/was a child |
| 誰{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Whoever it may be/have been |
| いずれに{しろ/せよ} | Whichever it may be; at any rate |
(v) Adverb | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| ゆっくりに{しろ/せよ} | Even though something happens slowly |

examples.english: No matter who writes it, there can be absolutely no mistakes.
examples.japanese: 誰が書くに｛しろ/せよ｝、絶対間違いがあってはいけない。

examples.english: Whether you go or not, please give me a call later.
examples.japanese: 行くに｛しろ/せよ｝、行かないに｛しろ/せよ｝、後で電話を下さい。

examples.english: At any rate (literally: whatever it is), leaving the situation as it is won't solve the problem.
examples.japanese: 何に｛しろ/せよ｝、このままでは問題は解決しない。

examples.english: Even though it is just practice, you have to take it seriously.
examples.japanese: たとえ練習に｛しろ/せよ｝、真面目にやらなければならない。

examples.english: Although the degree may differ from country to country (literally: there may be differences in degree), there is no country without gender discrimination.
examples.japanese: 程度の差はあるにせよ、性差別のない国はないだろう。

examples.english: Even if (it's true that) taking the drug will not solve all your problems, in your case, you have to alleviate the symptoms ﬁrst (by taking it).
examples.japanese: 薬を飲むことですべての問題が解決はしないにしろ、あなたの場合は薬で症状を軽減させることが先決です。

examples.english: Even if we ask someone to write it for us, we will have to think of what to say (literally: the content) ourselves.
examples.japanese: 誰かに書いてもらうにしろ、内容は我々が考えなければならない。

examples.english: Whichever software application you use, you must quickly get comfortable using it (literally: get used to how to use it).
examples.japanese: どのソフトを使うにしろ、早く使い方に慣れてもらわないといけない。

examples.english: Whoever explains it (to him) must be very careful not to hurt his feelings.
examples.japanese: 誰がそれを説明するにせよ、相手の気持ちを傷つけないように細心の注意が必要だ。

examples.english: No matter what the circumstances were, quitting the job without saying anything is just (too) irresponsible.
examples.japanese: どんな事情があったにせよ、何も言わずに仕事を辞めるのは無責任すぎる。

examples.english: Books on Web page design are spilling off of bookstore shelves, and whether we want to read them ourselves or recommend them to someone else, it is hard to know what to choose.
examples.japanese: ホームページの制作に関する書籍は書店の棚にあふれている状態で、自分が読むにせよ、他人に勧めるにせよ、大いに迷う。

examples.english: First of all, whether you support the current administration or criticize it, an accurate understanding and a cool analysis of the problems are indispensable.
examples.japanese: 現政権を支持するにせよ批判するにせよ、まずはじめに問題に対する正確な理解と冷静な分析が不可欠である。

examples.english: Whether it be baseball or soccer, you cannot stay as a professional player just with an ordinary effort.
examples.japanese: 野球にせよサッカーにせよ、プロでやっていくには並の努力では続かない。

examples.english: Whether they do it consciously or unconsciously, ordinary people try to avoid unpleasant things.
examples.japanese: 普通の人は、意識的にせよ無意識的にせよ、不快なことを避けようとする。

examples.english: Whether it is true or not, once you send out information on the Internet, you can't take it back.
examples.japanese: 一旦ネットに発信してしまった情報は、それが真実にせよそうでないにせよ、取り消しができない。

points.explanation: にしろ・せよ A conjunctive phrase that carries the meaning of concession.
points.meaning: Even though (it is/was the case that); even if (it is true that); although (it is/was the case that); whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.; whether X or Y

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Vinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| {行く/行った}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though someone goes/went |
(ii) Adjectiveいinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| {高い/高かった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was expensive |
(iii) Adjectiveなstem | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | |
| 不十分{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was insufficient |
(iv) Noun | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | |
| 子供{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though it is/was a child |
| 誰{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Whoever it may be/have been |
| いずれに{しろ/せよ} | Whichever it may be; at any rate |
(v) Adverb | に{しろ/せよ} | |
| ゆっくりに{しろ/せよ} | Even though something happens slowly |

examples.english: He has studied Japanese for 20 years, but he told me that even he still encounters grammar he doesn't understand.
examples.japanese: 彼は日本語を20年も勉強しているが、その彼にしたところで、まだ分からない文法に時々出くわすそうだ。

examples.english: Children go (places) beyond their parents' reach sooner or later. You may think that your own children will be different, but they, too, will be the same.
examples.japanese: 子供はいつか手の届かないところへ行ってしまうものだ。自分の子だけはそうでないと思うかもしれないが、あなたの子にしたところで同じだ。

examples.english: My husband, whose past affair was discovered, turned deﬁant, saying, ""It was 10 years ago, so it's too late (to do anything)"" I, too, couldn't bear to go forward with a divorce when I thought about our two children.
examples.japanese: 昔の浮気が発覚した夫は「10年たってるんだからもう時効だ」と開き直りの態度です。私にしたところで二人の子供のことを考えると離婚にはなかなか踏み切れません。

examples.english: Lately, you seldom see people writing with a fountain pen, and that makes me feel terribly disappointed. But even I usually use a ball-point pen.
examples.japanese: 最近は万年筆で字を書く人というのを、ほとんど見なくなって残念だ。もっとも、そういう私にしたところで、普段使っているのはボールペンだ。

examples.english: Yukio Mishima wrote that he remembered (literally: had a memory of) taking his ﬁrst bath as a baby, but there's no way even he remembered everything he did from birth until death (literally: until he died).
examples.japanese: 三島由紀夫は産湯に浸かった記憶があると書いているが、彼にしたところで、死ぬまでのすべての記憶があるわけではない。

points.explanation: A compound particle that means "even" or "also".
points.meaning: Also; (even) for ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | にしたところで | |
| その教授にしたところで | The professor is also ~/even the professor |

examples.english: Excessive fear and worry will make your hair turn grey overnight.
examples.japanese: 過度の恐怖や心労が一夜にして白髪をつくる。

examples.english: She had her ﬁrst child at the age of 45.
examples.japanese: 彼女は45歳にして初めて子供ができた。

examples.english: We can now watch live TV broadcasts from Japan while in a foreign country.
examples.japanese: 外国に居ながらにして日本からの生のテレビ放送が見られるようになった。

examples.english: An air raid turned the city of Tokyo into a burnt ﬁeld overnight.
examples.japanese: 空襲で東京の町は一夜にして焼け野原になってしまった。

examples.english: The sales of this book began to decline visibly a week after it went on sale.
examples.japanese: この本は発売1週間にして売れ行きが目に見えて落ち込み始めた。

examples.english: As expected of a child born of a handsome couple, the baby girl developed striking features one month after her birth.
examples.japanese: 美男美女のカップルの子にふさわしく、その女の子は生後1か月にして目鼻立ちがはっきりしていた。

examples.english: Kepler obtained a secure position and income at a young age, and was given the opportunity to devote his entire life to astronomy research.
examples.japanese: ケプラーは若年にして地位と収入の安定を獲得し、生涯天文学の研究に打ち込む機会をも与えられたのだった。

examples.english: He's in such a hurry! He started to keep a journal for college entrance examinations while still a freshman in high school.
examples.japanese: 彼はなんと気の早いことに、高校１年にして大学受験日記をつけ始めた。

examples.english: This year, on my second try, I passed Level 1 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test.
examples.japanese: 今年受験2回目にして日本語能力試験1級に合格した。

examples.english: When I think about it now it makes me smile, but when I was young I worried about every little thing under the sun.
examples.japanese: 今にして思えば懐かしいが、若い頃は小さなことでもくよくよ悩んでいたねえ。

examples.english: I have heard that people are born with the ability to live in good health.
examples.japanese: 人間は生まれながらにして健康に生きていこうとする力を持っているそうだ。

examples.english: Rome was not built in a day.
examples.japanese: ローマは一日にして成らず。

examples.english: At the age of 40 one doesn't doubt, and at 50 one knows heaven's will. (The Analects of Confucius)
examples.japanese: 四十にして惑わず。五十にして天命を知る。（『論語』）

points.explanation: にして (1) A compound particle that indicates a period of time/stage (in life) at which some surprising action or state takes place.
points.meaning: In; at; over; while

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Number+Counter | にして | |
| 三歳にして | When someone is three years old |
| 大学四年にして恋を知る | Someone falls in love for the first time when he/she is a senior in college |
(ii) Noun | にして | |
| 一昼夜にして | Something changes in 24 hours (literally: one day and one night) |
(iii) Vますながら | にして | |
| 生まれながらにして | When someone is born |

examples.english: She is a bright and also beautiful secretary.
examples.japanese: 彼女は頭脳明晰にして端麗な秘書である。

examples.english: He was both a distinguished scholar and an excellent educator.
examples.japanese: 彼は偉大な学者にして優れた教育者でもあった。

examples.english: (The character of) That man is boorish and ﬁerce.
examples.japanese: あの男の性格は粗野にして猛々しい。

examples.english: The Prime Minister's condition is unstable and unpredictable.
examples.japanese: 首相の容体は不安定にして、予断を許さない。

examples.english: The politician was a man of principle, purity and nobility.
examples.japanese: その政治家は志操堅固にして、高潔清廉な人だった。

examples.english: No crime could be as ingenious and perfect as this one.
examples.japanese: これほど巧妙にして完璧な犯罪はないでしょう。

examples.english: Her paintings have become phenomenally popular (literally: gathered overwhelming support) for their elaborate and light-hearted brush strokes.
examples.japanese: 彼女の絵は緻密にして軽やかな筆づかいで圧倒的な支持を集めた。

examples.english: That grammar dictionary has clear, detailed explanations.
examples.japanese: あの文法辞典は詳細にして明解な説明が施されている。

examples.english: This is a solid and simple (example of) folk art.
examples.japanese: これは堅牢にして素朴な民芸品であります。

examples.english: All of this director's ﬁlms are gloomy and sad.
examples.japanese: この監督の映画はすべて陰鬱にして物悲しい。

examples.english: The way that politician speaks and acts deﬁes common sense, and he is criticized endlessly.
examples.japanese: あの政治家の言動は非常識にして、絶えず批判されている。

examples.english: Eita is (a man who is) stubborn of spirit, and is never taken advantage of by others.
examples.japanese: 栄太は内心頑固にして決して人に使われる男ではない。

examples.english: He is a superb researcher and a fervent educator.
examples.japanese: 彼は優秀な研究者にして熱烈な教育者でもある。

points.explanation: にして (2) A conjunction meaning "and" that is used to combine two noun phrases or な-adjectives.
points.meaning: And; both ~ and ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Number+Counter | にして | |
| 三歳にして | When someone is three years old |
| 大学四年にして恋を知る | Someone falls in love for the first time when he/she is a senior in college |
(ii) Noun | にして | |
| 一昼夜にして | Something changes in 24 hours (literally: one day and one night) |
(iii) Vますながら | にして | |
| 生まれながらにして | When someone is born |

examples.english: I am not a soccer fan, but during the World Cup, even I got excited.
examples.japanese: ワールドカップの時はサッカーファンでもない私にしてからが興奮状態でした。

examples.english: Even the police don't protect citizens from violence unless an incident actually occurs.
examples.japanese: 警察にしてからが、いざ事件が起きないと市民を暴力から守ってくれない。

examples.english: In Greek or Roman sculptures and mural paintings there are no emaciated-looking women. Even Venus, the Goddess of Beauty, is quite full-ﬁgured.
examples.japanese: ギリシャやローマの彫刻や壁画などに、痩せた女性は皆無だ。美の女神、ヴィーナスにしてからが、かなり太めだ。

examples.english: Even he, the greatest intellectual of the day, was deceived by love.
examples.japanese: 当代随一の知性人である彼にしてからが、恋愛にたぶらかされている。

examples.english: He produced paintings in the mode he inherited from his father, but that style was already considered outdated in his father's time.
examples.japanese: 息子は父から受け継いだ作風で作品を描いていたが、すでにその父にしてからが、古くさいと言われていた。

examples.english: Even the prime minister's plan for structural reform met with strong resistance from bureaucrats.
examples.japanese: 首相の構造改革案にしてからが、官僚の強い抵抗にあっている。

points.explanation: A compound particle indicating that something unexpected occurs.
points.meaning: even

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | にしてからが | |
| 首相にしてからが | Even the prime minister |

examples.english: Even if we decide to buy a piano, we won't have a place to put it in such a small apartment.
examples.japanese: ピアノを買うにしても、こんな狭いアパートでは置くところがない。

examples.english: Even though (we agree that) Miki's story was exaggerated, probably not all of it was untrue.
examples.japanese: 美紀の言ったことは大げさだったにしても、すべてがウソというわけではないだろう。

examples.english: No matter who is going to do this job, we have no room for mistakes.
examples.japanese: 誰がこの仕事をやるにしても失敗は許されない。

examples.english: Whether you go or someone else does, this meeting will take a lot of preparation.
examples.japanese: 君が行くにしても他の誰かが行くにしても今回の会議はかなりの準備が必要だ。

examples.english: With honorific language, too, we often notice incorrect usage these days.
examples.japanese: 敬語の使い方にしても近頃は間違った言い方が目につく。

examples.english: Even if we (decide to) go home right now, I wonder if we will be able to get plane tickets.
examples.japanese: 今すぐ帰るにしても、飛行機の切符が取れるだろうか。

examples.english: Kyoto has so many places to see, so even if you (decide to) stay within the city, you should plan on spending about three days.
examples.japanese: 京都は見るところがたくさんあるので、市内だけ回るにしても3日くらいとっておいた方がいいでしょう。

examples.english: Even taking the strong inﬂuence from China into account, this work demonstrates the high quality craftsmanship of Japanese painters.
examples.japanese: この作品は中国大陸の影響が濃厚であるにしても、日本の画工の高い水準を示している。

examples.english: Even though (it is true that) we could avoid a worst-case scenario, the damage from this typhoon is (still) enormous.
examples.japanese: 今度の台風では最悪の事態は避けられたにしても、被害は甚大だ。

examples.english: Even though it's not what you get in New York, you can listen to fairly high-quality music in this city, too.
examples.japanese: ニューヨークほどではないにしても、この市でもかなり質の高い音楽が聴けます。

examples.english: Whatever you may do (in the future), you'd do well to study English hard.
examples.japanese: 何をするにしても英語はしっかり勉強しておいた方がいい。

examples.english: Whether you decide to go or not, could you make up your mind soon?
examples.japanese: 行くにしてもやめるにしても早く決めてもらえませんか。

examples.english: When he said that, Tatsuya didn't intend to be mean-spirited, either.
examples.japanese: 達也にしても悪気があってあんなことを言ったわけじゃない。

examples.english: Because most of the appliances in imported campers are designed for the 120-volt standard, stoves and air-conditioners, for example, do not have enough output at campsites in Japan, where 100 volts is the standard.
examples.japanese: 輸入キャンピングカー車内器具はほとんどが１２０Vの規格で作られているので、１００V電源の日本のキャンプ場ではレンジにしてもエアコンにしても、今一つ出力が弱い。

points.explanation: A conjunction that represents the idea of "even if someone decides to do something," or "even if/though someone decides that something is true/the case".
points.meaning: Even if (someone decides to/it is true that); although/even though (it is true that/it is the case that/we admit that/we agree that/etc.); whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.; whether X or Y; as for ~, too; even (so)

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Sinformal | にしても | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun is omitted |
| {行く/行った}にしても | Even if someone decides to go/even though (it is the case that) someone went |
| {高い/高かった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) something is expensive/even though (it is true that) something was expensive |
| 便利{∅/である/ だった/であった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) something is convenient/even though (it is true that) something was convenient |
| 学生{∅/である/ だった/であった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) someone is a student/even though (it is true that) someone was a student |
(ii) NP | にしても | |
| この国の文化にしても | This country’s culture, too |

examples.english: His area of research is not limited merely to philosophy, but extends to cognitive psychology as well.
examples.japanese: 彼の研究範囲は哲学(だけ)にとどまらず、認知心理学の領域にまで広がっている。

examples.english: Not only does she avidly read novels, she also has written a couple of novels herself, which have been published in magazines.
examples.japanese: 彼女は小説を広く読む(だけ)にとどまらず、自分でもいくつか書いて、すでに雑誌に発表している。

examples.english: The doctor is doing excellent research not only in his speciality, mathematics, but also in computer science.
examples.japanese: 博士は専門の数学にとどまらず、コンピュータサイエンスでも優れた研究をしている。

examples.english: At our lab, we don't just focus on theory, we also emphasize its application.
examples.japanese: 本研究室での研究は、単なる理論にとどまらず、その応用も重視している。

examples.english: My senior schoolmates, as people more experienced in life, have given me invaluable advice, not only when I was a student but also after I graduated.
examples.japanese: 先輩方には単に学生時代にとどまらず、卒業後も人生のよき先輩として貴重なアドバイスをいただいてまいりました。

examples.english: This medical school not only teaches technical expertise, it also makes an effort to teach ethics (literally: human education), such as respect (literally: love) for human beings, a sense of mission and a sense of responsibility.
examples.japanese: 本医学部は医学の専門知識だけにとどまらず、人間愛、使命感、責任感、といった人間教育にも力を注いでいます。

examples.english: In chamber music, each player has to understand not only his or her own part, but everyone else's as well.
examples.japanese: 室内楽では一人一人の奏者が自分のパートを理解するだけにとどまらず、他のすべてのパートも理解しなければならない。

examples.english: Not only does this medicine prevent your hair from thinning, it brings your grey hair back to its original black colour.
examples.japanese: この薬は髪が薄くなるのを防ぐだけにとどまらず、白髪を黒い髪に戻します。

examples.english: A doctorate from this university not only serves as evidence of excellence in professional knowledge, it also declares that the holder possesses great potential as a person.
examples.japanese: 本学の博士号は専門的知識における卓越性を証明するものであるにとどまらず、取得者が人間的力量の持ち主であることを宣言するものです。

examples.english: The field of mechanics is important not only as a system of science and technology that controls the material world, but also as a system for understanding the world.
examples.japanese: 力学という学問は、物質世界を統制する科学技術の体系として重要であるにとどまらず、世界を認識するための体系として重要である。

examples.english: Not only are her lectures interesting, they always have some deep philosophical meaning, too.
examples.japanese: 彼女の講演はただ面白いだけにとどまらず、必ず深い哲学が含まれている。

points.explanation: A phrase indicating that something goes beyond a spatial/temporal boundary.
points.meaning: Doesn’t stop with ~; doesn’t end with ~; not limited to ~; going beyond ~; not only ~ (but also ~)

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun(だけ) | にとどまらず | |
| 日本(だけ) にとどまらず | Something is not limited to Japan, and ~ |
| その時代(だけ) にとどまらず | Something goes beyond that age ~ |
(ii) Vinformal(だけ) | にとどまらず | |
| {読む/読んだ}(だけ) にとどまらず | Not only does/did someone read something, but ~ |
(iii) {Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | であるにとどまらず | |
| 証明するものであるにとどまらず | Something not only serves as evidence |
| 重要であるにとどまらず | Something is not only important |
(iv) Adjectiveいinformal | だけにとどまらず | |
| 面白いだけにとどまらず | Something is not only interesting |

examples.english: When I see the photo of my parents I took in Naples, I remember what a great time we had on that trip.
examples.japanese: ナポリで撮った両親の写真を見るにつけ、あの時の楽しかった旅行を思い出す。

examples.english: As I smell the scent of fresh green foliage, I tell myself it's finally spring and feel really relaxed, almost without realizing it.
examples.japanese: 新緑の香りを嗅ぐにつけ、「ああ、春なんだなあ」と思わずのほほんとしてしまいます。

examples.english: As I listen to the pianist's deeply-felt music and sense his warm personality, I feel strongly that music is man.
examples.japanese: そのピアニストの深みのある音楽を聴き、温かい人柄に触れるにつけ、「音楽は人なり」の思いを強くしております。

examples.english: As I watch the government's inability to deal with the increasingly serious problems related to the pension system and economy, I think that we must (do what we can to) protect ourselves.
examples.japanese: 深刻化する年金問題や経済問題に対する政府の無策ぶりを見るにつけ、自分のことは自分で守るしかないと思う。

examples.english: As I watch or hear about young people who are well over 20 but have no prospects for becoming independent, I feel heavy-hearted.
examples.japanese: 二十歳をはるかに過ぎても自立への見通しのつかない若者を見るにつけ、聞くにつけ、やるせない思いがあります。

examples.english: Whenever I think about the unhappy circumstances surrounding children, with the recent cases of bullying, abuse, and gruesome incidents, it makes me feel concerned about the future of this country.
examples.japanese: いじめや虐待、陰惨な事件など、子供を取り巻く不幸な状況を考えるにつけ、この国の行く末を案じずにはいられない。

examples.english: As I watch the wars going on in various places around the world, my heart aches.
examples.japanese: 世界各地での戦いの様子を見るにつけ胸が痛む。

examples.english: Whenever I read articles about all of the medical errors that have been happening (frequently) recently, I shudder at the thought that I could have been a victim.
examples.japanese: 最近頻発している医療ミスの記事を読むにつけ、私も被害者になる可能性があったのではと戦慄を覚えてしまう。

examples.english: As I feel the end of the year coming at a dash, I become aware of my age.
examples.japanese: 年末が一気に駆け足でやってくるのを感じるにつけ、自分の年齢を思い知らされます。

points.explanation: A conjunction indicating that each time someone perceives something he/she feels or thinks something associated with it.
points.meaning: As; every time; whenever

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Vinformal nonpast | につけ | Where V=verb of cognition |
| 景色を見るにつけ | As I look at the scenery |
| 日記を読むにつけ | As I read the diary |
| そのことを考えるにつけ | As I think about it |
| 年を感じるにつけ | As I become conscious of my age |
| その香りを嗅ぐにつけ | As I smell the scent |

examples.english: The Olympic Games were held for sixteen days.
examples.japanese: オリンピックが16日間にわたって開かれた。

examples.english: Due to the drought, crops were damaged over a wide area.
examples.japanese: 干ばつのため広範囲にわたって作物が被害を受けた。

examples.english: Due to work on the pipes, the water supply will be cut off from 1 a.m. to about 9 a.m. tomorrow.
examples.japanese: 配管工事のため、明日午前１時から午前9時ごろにわたって断水する。

examples.english: The articles appeared serially in the newspaper over eight issues (literally: extending to eight times).
examples.japanese: その記事は8回にわたって新聞に連載された。

examples.english: The Cold War, which lasted for about 40 years, ﬁnally came to an end.
examples.japanese: 約40年にわたる冷戦がついに終わった。

examples.english: Last night there was an interruption (literally: connection difficulties) in Company A's mobile phone service in a certain area of Kanto for about six hours starting about 9 o'clock.
examples.japanese: A社の携帯電話サービスで、関東の一部で昨夜午後9時ごろから約6時間にわたって接続障害があった。

examples.english: From the time of its debut in 1950, the cartoon ""Peanuts"" has fascinated fans all over the world for over half a century.
examples.japanese: コミック『ピーナッツ』は、１９５０年に誕生して以来半世紀以上にわたって世界中のファンを魅了してきた。

examples.english: On both sides of the river, the forest stretches for 20 acres.
examples.japanese: その川の両側には２０エーカーにわたって森が広がっている。

examples.english: Thick clouds extend from Kanto to Kyushu.
examples.japanese: 厚い雨雲が関東から九州にわたって広がっている。

examples.english: It became evident that one party paid the other bribes ﬁve times during the past year.
examples.japanese: 昨年1年間に両者の間で5回にわたって賄賂の授受があったことが明らかになった。

examples.english: The murder site was searched many times.
examples.japanese: 殺人現場は再三にわたって捜査が行われた。

examples.english: Our inspection of the electrical system in used cars covers ﬁve points, including the ignition system and the battery. (literally: Our Company checks ﬁve points of used cars' electric systems, including the ignition system and the battery.)
examples.japanese: 当社では、中古車の電気装置を点火装置やバッテリーを含む５項目にわたってチェックいたします。

examples.english: Before the experiment there were detailed instructions regarding how to use the instruments.
examples.japanese: 実験の前に詳細にわたって器具の使い方の指示があった。

examples.english: At this conference many issues concerning environmental protection were discussed.
examples.japanese: 今回の会議では、環境保護の多岐にわたる問題について、議論が交わされた。

examples.english: Ensuring safety from the production stage through the consumption stage is an urgent matter.
examples.japanese: 生産段階から消費段階にわたる食品の安全性を確保することが急務だ。

points.explanation: にわたって・わたる A compound particle indicating that something takes place over a particular span of time or physical space.
points.meaning: For; over; extending; stretching; ranging; covering

| 十キロにわたって | Extending over 10 kilometers |
| 東海地方全体にわたって | Over the entire Tokai region |
(ii) Noun1からNoun2 | にわたって | |
| 一時から六時にわたって | From 1 o’clock to 6 o’clock |

(iii) (Noun1から)Noun2 | にわたるNoun3 | |

examples.english: There is no way to save this company without restructuring it.
examples.japanese: リストラによらず(に)この会社を救う方法はない。

examples.english: At this company, if you are capable, you will be given big assignments one after another, regardless of your educational qualiﬁcations.
examples.japanese: この会社では学歴によらず、実力があればどんどん大きい仕事をまかされる。

examples.english: Whatever it may be, if you have trouble, please consult me anytime.
examples.japanese: 何事によらず困ったことがあったらいつでも相談して下さい。

examples.english: (Regardless of) Whether it is domestically produced or imported, as a rule I do not eat beef.
examples.japanese: 国産(である)か輸入(である)かによらず牛肉は食べないことにしている。

examples.english: This company will interview you regardless of your experience (literally: whether or not you have experience.)
examples.japanese: この会社は経験のあるなしによらず面接してくれる。

examples.english: No matter what the weather (literally: whatever the weather is like), the game will be held as scheduled.
examples.japanese: 天候のいかんによらず試合は予定通り行われます。

examples.english: Regardless of who it is (literally: who takes the project), the project manager will be given special compensation.
examples.japanese: 誰がそのプロジェクトを担当するかによらず担当者には特別手当が支給される。

examples.english: The ideal is to resolve disputes without using armed force.
examples.japanese: 理想は武力によらず紛争を解決することだ。

examples.english: Mr. Yoshikawa was employed by another company without his former employer's help (literally: good ofﬁces).
examples.japanese: 吉川さんは勤務先の斡旋によらず別の会社に再就職した。

examples.english: This contract may not be altered without the agreement of both parties.
examples.japanese: 本契約が両者の合意によらずに変更されることはない。

examples.english: In this dance studio, students can begin at any time and anyone, regardless of experience, can join.
examples.japanese: 当ダンス教室は、いつからでも始められ、経験によらずどなたでもご参加いただけます。

examples.english: The salaries of this company's sales representatives are not dependent on their length of employment or age; they are always based on sales performance.
examples.japanese: 当社のセールスマンの給与は勤務年数や年齢によらず、常に販売実績を基に決定される。

examples.english: The distance between Q and R is always the same, regardless of where P is.
examples.japanese: QRの長さはPの位置によらず常に一定である。

examples.english: Anyone can take this standardized test, regardless of what university or school you attend or whether you are a university student or a professional.
examples.japanese: この標準テストは在籍する大学や学部によらず、また大学生であるか社会人であるかによらず、誰でも受けられます。

examples.english: No matter what job you have, you should always do the work sincerely.
examples.japanese: どんな仕事によらず、いつも誠実に務めなければいけない。

examples.english: Whether you own a few things or many, a well-organized space makes you feel good.
examples.japanese: 持ち物が多いか少ないかによらず、きちんと整理ができている部屋は気持ちいい。

points.explanation: A compound particle that means "without depending on".
points.meaning: Without; without ~ing; regardless of; independently of; without reference to; whether X or Y; whether X or not; whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | によらず | |
| 紹介によらず | Without introduction |
| 学生数によらず | Regardless of the number of students |
(ii) Wh-word (Noun/NP) | によらず | |
| 誰によらず | Whoever it may be (literally: regardless of who it is) |
| どんな仕事によらず | Whatever work it may be (literally: regardless of what kind of work it is) |
(iii) XかYか | によらず | Where X, Y=contrastive words; usually nonpast forms |
Noun1かNoun2 | 英語か日本語かによらず | Regardless of whether something is English or Japanese |
V1informalかV2informalか | 勝つか負けるかによらず | Regardless of whether someone wins or loses |
Adjectiveい1informalかAdjectiveい2informal | 高いか安いかによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or cheap |
Adjectiveな1stemかAdjectiveな2stem | 偶然か意図的かによらず | Regardless of whether something is accidental or intentional |
(iv) Xか{どう/ 否}か | によらず | |
| 存在するか{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something exists or not |
| 高いか{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or not |
| 偶然か{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something is coincidental or not |
| 学生か{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether someone is a student or not |
(v) X(affirmative)かX(negative)か | によらず | |
| 行くか行かないかによらず | Regardless of whether someone goes or not |
| 高いか高くないかによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or not |
| 偶然(である)か偶然でないかによらず | Regardless of whether something is coincidental or not |
| 英語(である)か英語でないかによらず | Regardless of whether something is English or not |
(vi) X(affirmative)+X(negative)か | によらず | Where X={V/Adjectiveい}informal; usually nonpast forms |
| 行く行かないによらず | Regardless of whether someone goes or not |
| うまいうまくないによらず | Regardless of whether something is good or poor (at going something) |
(vii) X+Y | によらず | Where X, Y=Adjectiveいinformal nonpast/Adjectiveなstem; Y=X’s antonym |
| 上手下手によらず | Regardless of whether someone is skillful or unskillful |
| うまい下手によらず | Regardless of whether someone is good or poor (at going something) |
(viii) {Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | であるなしによらず | |
| 会員であるなしによらず | Regardless of whether someone is a member or not |
| 経済的であるなしによらず | Regardless of whether something is economical nor not |
(ix) Nounのあるなし | によらず | |
| 学位のあるなしによらず | Regardless of whether someone has a degree or not |
(x) Nounのいかん | によらず | |
| 方法のいかんによらず | Regardless of the method (literally: regardless of what the method is) |

examples.english: One of the travel magazines said that hot springs are good for arthritis.
examples.japanese: その温泉は旅行雑誌によると神経痛にいいそうだ。

examples.english: According to Japanese law, generally, youths under 12 are not subject to arrest.
examples.japanese: 日本の法律によるとおおむね12歳未満の者は逮捕の対象にならない。

examples.english: Based on what I heard, (it appears that) tuition will go up next year.
examples.japanese: 聞いたところによると来年は授業料が上がるらしい。

examples.english: According to a newspaper poll, the approval rating for the Cabinet dropped sharply to 22 percent.
examples.japanese: 新聞の世論調査によると、内閣支持率は22%にまで急落したそうだ。

examples.english: According to my friend, May Day in Finland is a day when everyone, including students, joins in a festival to celebrate spring.
examples.japanese: 友達に聞いたところによると、フィンランドのメーデーは学生も集まって春を祝う祭りの日だそうだ。

examples.english: According to Dr. H, dogs may be able to feel the faint electromagnetic waves that people generate when they walk.
examples.japanese: H博士によると、犬は人間が歩く際に発する弱い電磁波を感じ取っている可能性があるという。

examples.english: According to government sources, the government plans to establish a panel that will study measures to cope with bioterrorism.
examples.japanese: 政府筋によると、政府はバイオテロリズムへの対策を研究する審議会を設置する予定であるという。

examples.english: According to the law, the purpose of insurance for care of the elderly is to make appropriate medical and welfare services accessible.
examples.japanese: 法律によると、介護保険は適切な医療および福祉サービスが受けられるようにすることを目的としています。

examples.english: According to the dictionary, two characters are used for sabishii, ""寂"", ""淋"".
examples.japanese: 辞書によると、「さびしい」には「寂しい」と「淋しい」の二つの漢字が使われている。

examples.english: According to the survey, those who inﬂict violence and abuse upon the elderly are most often the victim's family, friends or acquaintances.
examples.japanese: 調査によると、高齢者に対する暴力と虐待の加害者は、家族、友人あるいは知人であることが最も多い。

examples.english: According to the standards for disciplinary action, if a faculty or staff member driving under the inﬂuence (of alcohol) causes an accident resulting in serious injury or death, he or she will be dismissed.
examples.japanese: 懲戒処分基準によると、教職員が酒酔い運転で死亡・重傷事故を起こした場合は免職になる。

examples.english: According to my Korean friend, the number of the learners of Korean is increasing.
examples.japanese: 韓国人の友人によると、中国では韓国語学習者が増えているらしい。

points.explanation: A compound particle that is used to identify the source of information provided in the sentence.
points.meaning: According to; based on

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | によると | |
| {新聞/法律 /規則/辞書}によると | According to the newspaper/law/rule/dictionary |

examples.english: Our company does business not only in Japan but also in America, Europe, and elsewhere.
examples.japanese: 我が社は日本国内のみならず、アメリカやヨーロッパなどでもビジネス活動を行っております。

examples.english: Today's companies should not just pursue profits; they should also consider environmental protection issues in their production activities. (literally: they must perform production activities that take the environment into consideration as well.)
examples.japanese: これからの企業は単に利益を追求するのみならず、環境に配慮した生産活動を行わなければならない。

examples.english: As a human being, he should be ashamed of what he did. Not only that, it is clearly a criminal act.
examples.japanese: 彼のしたことは人間として恥ずべきことである。のみならず、それは明らかに犯罪行為だ。

examples.english: It is necessary to change not only the fee structure but the service system as well.
examples.japanese: 料金体系のみならず、サービス体制も改善する必要がある。

examples.english: The president's decision is being criticized heavily not only within the country but also abroad.
examples.japanese: 大統領の決定には国内のみならず、海外からも強い批判の声が上がっている。

examples.english: Not only is this company famous worldwide as a carbonated beverage manufacturer, it is even an American symbol (literally: one of the entities that symbolize the United States).
examples.japanese: この会社は炭酸飲料メーカーとして世界的に有名であるのみならず、アメリカ合衆国を象徴する存在の一つでさえある。

examples.english: Crimes of this kind have an enormous impact on citizens, not only economically but also psychologically, as they can completely deprive citizens of their post-retirement livelihoods (among other things).
examples.japanese: この種の犯罪は、老後の生活資金を根こそぎ奪うなど、市民への経済的な影響が甚大であるのみならず、精神的打撃も多大である。

examples.english: Technology specialists should not simply play a role as promoters of technological advancement; they should also be independent actors who bear a heavy (literally: strong) sense of responsibility for the effect of technology on people and on society.
examples.japanese: 技術者は単に技術の進歩の推進者であるのみならず、人類・社会に及ぼす技術の影響についても強い責任感を持つ自律的な行動者であるべきである。

examples.english: The production, the sale, and the use of illegal diesel oil are extremely serious acts of tax evasion. Not only that, these acts result in environmental pollution because they bring about an increase in toxic substances in the atmosphere via the exhaust from diesel cars.
examples.japanese: 不正軽油の製造・販売・使用は、極めて悪質な脱税行為である。のみならず、ディーゼル車の排気ガスは大気中の有害物質を増加させるなど、環境汚染の原因にもなっている。

examples.english: I was totally exhausted. My shoulders and neck were stiff, of course, and I was suffering from severe insomnia. Not only that, when I did finally fall asleep, I had many dreams. (From Dreams by Akutagawa Ryunosuke)
examples.japanese: 私はすっかり疲れていた。肩や頸の凝るのはもちろん、不眠症もかなり甚しかった。のみならず偶々眠ったと思うと、いろいろの夢を見勝ちだった。(芥川龍之介『夢』)

points.explanation: A phrase that is used in formal writing to mean "not only".
points.meaning: Not only ~ (but also ~); not only that

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun (Particle) | のみならず | |
| 学生のみならず | Not only students |
| アジアからのみならず | Not only from Asia |
(ii) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | のみならず | |
| 理解{する/しない}のみならず | Not only does someone (not) understanding something |
| {難しい/難しくない}のみならず | Not only is something (not) difficult |
(iii) {Adjectiveなstem/ Noun} | であるのみならず | |
| 不自然であるのみならず | Something is not only unnatural |
| 学者であるのみならず | Someone is not only a scholar |
(iv) Sentence1。 | のみならず、Sentence2。 | |
| この問題は難しい。のみならず、解決に時間もかかる。 | This problem is difficult. Not only that, it’ll take time to solve |

examples.english: It was so sweet that I ate one bite and left the rest.
examples.japanese: 甘いのなんのって私は一口食べて全部残してしまいました。

examples.english: They drank so much; they completely emptied ﬁve bottles of sake.
examples.japanese: 飲んだのなんのって彼らは5本の酒を全部空けてしまった。

examples.english: It was so itchy that I couldn't sleep all night.
examples.japanese: かゆいのなんのって一晩中寝られなかった。

examples.english: It was so heavy that even two people couldn't lift it.
examples.japanese: 重いのなんのって二人でも持ち上がりませんでした。

examples.english: If you want to experience the true charm of the ocean, try whale watching. When seen in real life, whales are so huge they take your breath away.
examples.japanese: 海の醍醐味を味わうなら、ホエールウォッチングだ。実際に見るクジラは、大きいのなんのって、すごい迫力だよ。

examples.english: I almost had it, but the line broke and the ﬁsh went back into the sea. It was really big, so I was so disappointed!
examples.japanese: もう少しで釣れたのに糸が切れて魚は海の中。結構大きかったので悔しかったのなんのって！

examples.english: A: How was the game? B: Oh, no, it was so terrible! I don't even want to talk about it.
examples.japanese: A:試合はどうだった？ B:いやもう、ひどいのなんのって、話したくもないよ。

examples.english: It's so inconvenient; it takes up to an hour to get to the nearest supermarket.
examples.japanese: 不便なのなんのって一番近くのスーパーに行くのに1時間もかかるんです。

examples.english: The Asahidake Mountains had just turned colours and were so beautiful. Without realizing it, I stared at them for a while, completely forgetting the time.
examples.japanese: 朝日岳の山々はちょうど見事に色づいていてきれいなのなんのって。思わず時間を忘れて、しばらく見入ってしまいました。

examples.english: I was so surprised that I couldn't even speak for a while.
examples.japanese: 驚いたのなんのって、しばらくは言葉も出なかった。

examples.english: I could see so well with this telescope; I could even see Saturn's rings clearly.
examples.japanese: この望遠鏡、よく見えるのなんのって土星の輪まではっきり見えたよ。

points.explanation: A phrase to emphasize that something/someone is/was in an extreme state or that someone does/did something to a great extent
points.meaning: So (~ that); so much/well (~ that); so ~ and

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | のなんのって | |
| {効く/効いた}のなんのって | Something is/was so effective that ~ |
| {速い/速かった}のなんのって | Something is/was so fast that ~ |
(ii) Adjectiveなstem{な/だった} | のなんのって | |
| 下手{な/だった}のなんのって | Someone is/was so bad at something that ~ |

examples.english: I am appalled by his lack of common sense.
examples.japanese: 私は彼の常識の無さにあきれている。

examples.english: I wanted to jump, but I couldn't. I became painfully aware of my lack of physical and muscular strength.
examples.japanese: 跳びたいと思っても跳べない。体力、筋力の無さを痛感しました。

examples.english: We cannot accept your company's response to this situation, and we are ﬁlled with anger at your company's lack of sincerity.
examples.japanese: 今回の一連の貴社の対応は、私たちには全く納得できるものではなく、貴社の誠意の無さに大変な憤りを感じます。

examples.english: Although I was allowed to use a dictionary, because of the time constraint there were parts I couldn't answer, and I felt depressed about my lack of English proﬁciency.
examples.japanese: 辞書の使用を許可してもらったものの、時間不足で思ったように答えられない問題があり、自分の英語力の無さに落ち込みました。

examples.english: Friendliness, warmth and a lack of affectation are what makes Saya so absolutely charming.
examples.japanese: 親しみやすさと、温かさと、飾り気の無さが、さやの絶対的な魅力である。

examples.english: I am disappointed with recent movies and dramas because of their lack of content.
examples.japanese: 最近の映画やドラマは、その内容の無さにがっかりさせられる。

examples.english: According to a survey, Japanese children are the least self-conﬁdent in the world.
examples.japanese: 調査によると日本の子供の自信の無さは世界一だそうである。

examples.english: This comic had an interesting plot, but as the story went on, it became so exaggerated that I couldn't take the lack of reality.
examples.japanese: このマンガは設定は面白かったが、物語が進むにつれて話が大きくなり、リアリティの無さについていけなくなってしまった。

points.explanation: の無さ・のなさ A phrase that indicates a state where something is lacking.
points.meaning: Lack of; absence of

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | の無さ | |
| 能力の無さ | Lack of ability |
| 元気の無さ | Lack of spirit |

examples.english: It is usually a professor who is to blame when his students don't comprehend what he tries to convey.
examples.japanese: 教授の言わんとすることが学生に伝わらないのは、たいてい教授の方が悪いのだ。

examples.english: The sun was about to sink behind the mountain ridge.
examples.japanese: 太陽はまさに山の稜線に沈まんとしていた。

examples.english: I don't comprehend what that politician is trying to say.
examples.japanese: あの政治家は言わんとしているところがよく分からない。

examples.english: Whenever someone tries to do something with good intentions, inevitably there is someone who discourages it.
examples.japanese: 善意で何事かを行わんとすると、必ずそれに水を差す人間がいる。

examples.english: I am fed up with overprotective scientists (literally: the overprotection of scientists) who try to eliminate non specialists.
examples.japanese: 専門家でない者を排除せんとする科学者の過剰防衛には辟易させられる。

examples.english: A person who is about to die gives vent to his true feelings.
examples.japanese: 死なんとする者は本音を吐くものだ。

examples.english: The trees are about to be blown over by the violent wind.
examples.japanese: 暴風のために木々が倒れんとしている。

examples.english: The moon, which was just about to shine, was concealed by the clouds.
examples.japanese: まさに輝かんとする月が雲で隠れた。

examples.english: At the castle tower, which was on the verge of collapse, stood the castle lord, ready to share its fate.
examples.japanese: 今にも崩れんとする天守閣には、城と命運をともにする城主の姿があった。

examples.english: There was heavy rain, mostly in and around Tokyo.
examples.japanese: 東京を中心に大雨が降った。

examples.english: Bird ﬂu is spreading rapidly, primarily in Southeast Asia.
examples.japanese: 東南アジアを中心に鳥インフルエンザが急速に広がっている。

examples.english: This research is progressing, with Professor Nakajima taking the lead.
examples.japanese: この研究は中島教授を中心に進められている。

examples.english: These days I mainly read business books, rather than novels.
examples.japanese: 最近は小説よりもビジネス書を中心に読んでいる。

examples.english: Company R, a fast food company, plans to open 25 new stores in Kobe and neighbouring cities before long.
examples.japanese: ファーストフードのR社は近々神戸を中心に新たに25店舗を開く予定だ。

examples.english: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology is taking the lead in investigating compulsory education reform.
examples.japanese: 現在、文部科学省を中心に、義務教育改革に向けた検討が進められている。

examples.english: It has become clear from a recent survey that the viewing of online videos is increasing in America- most notably among young people.
examples.japanese: 最近の調査で、アメリカでのオンラインビデオの視聴が若い層を中心に伸びていることが分かった。

examples.english: The computer manufacturer P announced that it would give a large price reduction of 20 percent or more for their computers, with desktop models as the primary target.
examples.japanese: コンピュータメーカーのP社はデスクトップモデルを中心に２０％以上の大幅値下げを行うと発表した。

examples.english: This website highlights Kumamoto news as well as information on hot springs, gourmet foods, events, etc.
examples.japanese: このサイトは熊本のニュースを中心に、温泉やグルメ、イベント情報などもご紹介します。

examples.english: In this project we examined primarily the interrelationship between language-based communication and non-linguistic factors, such as meter, motions, facial expressions, etc.
examples.japanese: 本プロジェクトでは、言語による情報伝達と、韻律や動作、表情など、言語以外の要素との関係を中心に研究を行った。

examples.english: This exhibition, focusing mainly on works by an eminent Japanese architect, introduces modern architecture in Tokyo.
examples.japanese: この展示会はある著名な日本の建築家の作品を中心に、東京に建てられたモダンな建築について紹介している。

points.explanation: A phrase that means "with something/someone at the centre".
points.meaning: Centering around; around; focusing on; mainly; primarily; with ~ as the center; with ~ as the leader; with ~ as the primary ~; take the lead

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Noun | を中心に | |
| 日本を中心に | Centering around Japan |

examples.english: We are negotiating the price with the manufacturer through a local agent now.
examples.japanese: 今、現地の代理人を介して製造元と価格の交渉をしている。

examples.english: Music and movies can be distributed via the Internet now.
examples.japanese: インターネットを介して音楽や映画を配信できるようになった。

examples.english: We are trying to promote interaction among the local (units) through volunteer activities.
examples.japanese: 我々はボランティア活動を介して地域の交流を図ろうとしている。

examples.english: Business talks via an interpreter are inefficient.
examples.japanese: 通訳を｛介しての/介した｝商談は効率が悪い。

examples.english: I got this information with the help of (literally: through) a friend of mine in Japan.
examples.japanese: 日本にいる友達を介してこの情報を手に入れた。

examples.english: This virus is transmitted to people from infected birds via mosquitoes. It is not transmitted between people either directly or via mosquitoes.
examples.japanese: このウイルスはそれに感染した鳥から蚊を介して人に感染する。人から人や人から蚊を介しての感染はない。

examples.english: There have been several incidents in which a man and a woman who had met through a suicide website committed suicide together right after meeting in person for the first time, and such incidents have become a social problem.
examples.japanese: 自殺系サイトを介して知り合った男女が、初対面でいきなり一緒に自殺するという事件が続き、社会問題となった。

examples.english: This terrorist organization seems to be collecting and distributing money via overseas ﬁnancial institutions.
examples.japanese: このテロ組織は海外の金融機関を介して資金の調達と仕送りをしているらしい。

examples.english: When we recall memories, they are reconstructed through the part of the brain called the hippocampus.
examples.japanese: 記憶は再生時に脳の「海馬」という部分を介して再構成される。

examples.english: It is said that more ideas for creating new business can be obtained via informal communication outside of work.
examples.japanese: 新しいビジネスを生むためのアイデアは、勤務外のインフォーマルなコミュニケーションを介して、より多く得られると言われる。

examples.english: This group provides various kinds of support so that people with the same sort of disorder or disability can better understand others' problems and help each other by interacting.
examples.japanese: このグループは、同じような障害で悩んでいる人々が、お互いの交流を介して問題をよりよく理解し、助け合っていけるよう、様々な支援を行っている。

| 通信網を{介しての/介した}データ送信 | Data transmission via a network |

examples.english: I cannot hold back my anger at such an irresponsible deed.
examples.japanese: このような無責任な行いに対して怒りを禁じ得ない。

examples.english: Seeing the moving scene, I could not keep my tears from welling up.
examples.japanese: その感動的な光景を見て、涙がこみ上げてくるのを禁じ得なかった。

examples.english: (Seeing) the family reunited, an occasion that finally became reality after twenty-four years of agony and separation, people around them couldn't help but cry, too.
examples.japanese: 24年の苦悩と空白の後、ついに実現した家族との再会に、周囲の者も涙を禁じ得なかった。

examples.english: Looking at the beautiful early spring landscape painting, I felt the painter's love for his homeland, and couldn't help but be moved profoundly.
examples.japanese: その美しい早春の風景画に作者の温かい郷土愛を感じ、深い感動を禁じ得なかった。

examples.english: I can't hold back my surprise and anger at the publisher's thoughtless way of treating those personal photos.
examples.japanese: 出版社による無神経な個人写真の扱い方に、驚きと憤りを禁じ得ない。

examples.english: I cannot keep myself from wondering if the president's announcement will pour cold water on the two nations' hard-won first step toward peaceful uniﬁcation.
examples.japanese: 大統領の声明は、せっかく第一歩を踏み出した両国の平和統一の働きに水を差すのではないかという疑問を禁じ得ない。

examples.english: As the moment approached when I was to meet with the person I'd admired for a long time, I could not stop my heart from beating faster and faster.
examples.japanese: 長い間憧れていた人に会う瞬間が近づいて、次第に動悸が速まるのを禁じ得なかった。

examples.english: (Looking at) this industry's hopeless conservatism, I couldn't help but let out a deep sigh.
examples.japanese: この業界の救いようのない保守性に、深いため息が出るのを禁じ得なかった。

points.meaning: Cannot hold; cannot hold back; cannot keep back; cannot help ~ing; cannot keep ~ from ~ing

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | を禁じ得ない | |
| 喜びを禁じ得ない | Cannot keep back one’s joy |
(ii) Vinformal nonpastの | を禁じ得ない | |
| 足が震えるのを禁じ得ない | Cannot keep someone’s legs from trembling |

examples.english: Citizens' opinions are divided over the monorail construction.
examples.japanese: モノレール建設をめぐって市民の意見が対立している。

examples.english: (Voices of) Criticism concerning wasteful public projects is growing stronger.
examples.japanese: 無駄な公共事業をめぐる批判の声が強まっている。

examples.english: Opinions were exchanged actively regarding how universities should be run from now on.
examples.japanese: 大学運営は今後どうあるべきかをめぐって活発に意見が交わされた。

examples.english: There was a heated discussion over whether we should advance or retreat.
examples.japanese: 進攻か撤退かをめぐって激しい議論が戦わされた。

examples.english: Opinions were divided among the committee members regarding whether we should shift to the new system immediately or wait until next year.
examples.japanese: 新制度に即時切り替えるべきか来年度まで待つべきかをめぐって委員の間で意見が分かれた。

examples.english: The ﬁerce debate over the new history textbook continues.
examples.japanese: 新しい歴史教科書をめぐって激しい議論が続いている。

examples.english: The players had a ﬁght over the umpire's decision, and the game was interrupted for about an hour.
examples.japanese: 審判の判定をめぐって選手が乱闘し試合が約１時間中断した。

examples.english: There were ﬁerce arguments over the pros and cons of dispatching the Self-Defence Forces.
examples.japanese: 自衛隊派遣の是非をめぐって激しい議論が交わされた。

examples.english: Research into the mechanism of aging is drawing a lot of attention.
examples.japanese: 老化のメカニズムをめぐる研究が注目を浴びている。

examples.english: It looks like the movement toward IT (information technology) will accelerate in our prefecture, too.
examples.japanese: 我が県でもITをめぐる働きが加速しそうです。

examples.english: This chapter introduces recent trends in nuclear power generation and gives an overview of promising energy sources for the future.
examples.japanese: 本章では、原子力発電をめぐる最近の動向を紹介すると共に、将来の有力なエネルギー源について概観する。

examples.english: Just when the army should be withdrawn is hotly debated in other countries, too.
examples.japanese: 他の国でもいつ軍隊を引き上げるべきかをめぐって議論が戦わされている。

examples.english: While there are reports almost every day on juvenile crime, which is becoming more serious, society wavers between applying strict punishment and emphasizing rehabilitation.
examples.japanese: 深刻化する少年犯罪が連日のように報道されている中、厳罰主義か更生重視かをめぐって社会の対応が揺れている。

examples.english: Our opinions are divided over whether we should accept the arbitration plan or continue negotiating.
examples.japanese: 調停案を受け入れるかこのまま交渉を続けるかをめぐって我々の間で意見が分かれている。

points.explanation: をめぐって・めぐる A compound particle meaning "concerning; over", which is used with an issue over which different opinions, ideas, etc., are expressed or exchanged.
points.meaning: Centering around; in connection with; over; concerning; regarding; with regard to

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | をめぐって | |
| この報道をめぐって | Concerning this news report |
(ii) Noun1 | をめぐるNoun2 | |
| 基礎研究をめぐる現状 | Current status of (literally: around) basic research |
(iii) Embedded Question | をめぐって | |
| 日本がこの問題にどう対応するべきかをめぐって | Regarding how Japan should handle this problem |
(iv) Noun1かNoun2か | をめぐって | |
| 実行か中止かをめぐって | Concerning whether we should execute something, or hold off on it |
(v) Embedded Question1+Embedded Question2 | をめぐって | |
| 単独で行うかパートナーを探すかをめぐって | Regarding whether we want to do it by ourselves or look for a partner |

examples.english: When I come to think of it, I had a great time when I was in college.
examples.japanese: 思えば、大学時代はとても楽しかった。

examples.english: When I think back, I discussed political issues with him almost every day.
examples.japanese: 思えば、あの頃私は彼と政治問題について毎日のように議論したものだ。

examples.english: Come to think of it, for a few years after the war, almost all Japanese people grew vegetables in their backyards.
examples.japanese: 思えば、終戦後数年は、ほとんどの日本人が野菜を庭で育てていた。

examples.english: Now that I think about it, why did I buy such a (terrible) CD?
examples.japanese: 今思えばどうしてこんなCDを買ったのだろう。

examples.english: Come to think of it, there were warning signs of a cardiac seizure.
examples.japanese: 思えば心筋梗塞の前兆はあった。

examples.english: I saw a movie in Ginza with my grandmother when I was a third grader. When I think back on it now, that was the first and the last movie I ever saw with her.
examples.japanese: 小学校3年生の時、祖母と銀座で映画を見た。今にして思えば、あれが祖母と見た最初で最後の映画だった。

examples.english: As I think of it now, my father was vehemently opposed when I told him that I was going to marry my colleague. I regret that I didn't listen to his advice.
examples.japanese: 今から思えば、私が同僚の男性と結婚すると言った時、父は猛然と反対した。あの時父の忠告を聞いておけばと悔やまれる。

examples.english: The moment I went out on my bicycle, the chain came off. When I come to think of it now, that was the beginning of (a period of) bad luck.
examples.japanese: 自転車で出かけようとした途端、チェーンが外れてしまった。今から思えば、あれがケチのつき始めだった。

points.explanation: An adverb that indicates feelings of nostalgia or regret when recollecting one’s past experiences.
points.meaning: Come ot think of it; when I think back; on reflection

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

examples.english: Despite severe physical handicaps, she took charge of her own life.
examples.japanese: 彼女は重度の身体障害をものともせず、自分の人生をつかみとった。

examples.english: Undaunted by his inability to speak Japanese, he travelled around Japan communicating with gestures and signs.
examples.japanese: 彼は日本語がしゃべれないのをものともせず、身振り手振りで日本を旅行して歩いた。

examples.english: Overcoming high waves, my friend swam (all of) four kilometres.
examples.japanese: 友人は高波をものともせず4キロを泳ぎ切った。

examples.english: In spite of the time difference, my child changed to her swimming suit right away and went to Waikiki Beach.
examples.japanese: 子供は時差をものともせず、早速水着に着替えてワイキキビーチへ出かけた。

examples.english: At the time of the high-rise fire, firemen ran up the stairs of the building in spite of the danger.
examples.japanese: 高層ビル火災の際、消防士たちは危険をものともせずその建物の階段を駆け登っていった。

examples.english: The people continued their demonstrations in deﬁance of the military government's oppression.
examples.japanese: 民衆は軍事政権の弾圧をものともせず、デモ行進を続けた。

examples.english: Ignoring criticism from the people around her, she proceeded on the path she believed in.
examples.japanese: 彼女は周囲の人の批判をものともせず、自分の信じる道を進んだ。

examples.english: The high school students were practicing baseball in spite of the heavy rain (literally: in spite of the fact that it was raining hard).
examples.japanese: 高校生たちは雨が激しく降っているのをものともせず、熱心に野球の練習をしていた。

examples.english: Despite the fact that it took Misako two hours each way, she commuted (every day) to a securities company in Tokyo.
examples.japanese: 美佐子は片道所要時間が2時間を越えるのをものともせず、東京の証券会社に通勤した。

points.explanation: A phrase indicating that someone does something bravely/fearlessly in spite of unfavourable circumstances.
points.meaning: In spite of ~; undaunted by ~; in definance of ~; in the face of ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun | をものともせず | |
| 失敗をものともせず | In spite of the failure |
(ii) Sinformalの | をものともせず | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun changes to な |
| 非難されたのをものともせず | In spite of the fact that someone was criticised |
| 頭が痛いのをものともせず | In spite of the fact that someone has a headache |
| 場所が不便{な/である}のをものともせず | In spite of the fact that the location is inconvenient |
| 夫が病気{な/である}のをものともせず | In spite of the fact that someone’s husband is ill |

examples.english: In my view, culture is a kind of religion.
examples.japanese: (私が)思うに、文化は宗教の一種だ。

examples.english: Considering the nature of the medical world, I believe there is collusion between doctors and pharmaceutical companies.
examples.japanese: 医学界の体質を思うに、当然医者と製薬会社の癒着はあると思う。

examples.english: In my view, the present state is that the media, which distribute information, and the citizens, who receive it, are completely separate and static.
examples.japanese: 思うに、情報を発信するマスコミと受信する我々国民は、完全に分化され固定化されてしまっているのが現状だ。

examples.english: I can think of nothing less pleasurable than a life devoted to pleasure. ― John D. Rockefeller, Jr.
examples.japanese: 「思うに、快楽に耽る人生ほど快楽から遠いものはない。」ージョン・D・ロックフェラー2世

examples.english: I would recommend joining a club activity at college. I'm sure it would be something you'd treasure for the rest of your life.
examples.japanese: 私が思うに、大学時代の部活はお薦めだ。きっと一生の宝物になるだろう。

examples.english: It seems to me that even an outstanding painter can create dynamic artworks only during a certain period of his or her life.
examples.japanese: 思うに、優れた画家であっても、生命感あふれる作品を生み出せるのはほんの一時期ではないだろうか。

examples.english: In my view, people who excel at getting things from others (literally: using people) are unattractive people.
examples.japanese: 思うに、「人を使う」ことが上手な人間というのは魅力のない人間である。

examples.english: When I reﬂect upon my past, it appears to me that my constant sense of curiosity in everything has served as a driving power for me to keep on doing my research.
examples.japanese: 自分の来し方を思うに、常に幅広い好奇心を持ち続けてきたことが、研究を続ける原動力ではなかっただろうか。

examples.english: It's painful not to be able to do anything when I think about the circumstances of people who were hit by the earthquake.
examples.japanese: 大地震の被災者の人たちの状況を思うに、何もできずにいることが本当につらいです。

points.explanation: A phrase indicating that the subsequent statement is the speaker’s/writer’s personal view.
points.meaning: In my view; it seems to me that ~; when I think (about ~); considering

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) 思うに、 | Sentence。 | |
| 思うに、コンピュータは良し悪しだ。 | In my view computers are good and bad |
(ii) NPを | 思うに | |
| この一年を思うに、つらいことが多かった。 | When I think about this past year, it was full of trying things |

examples.english: If you want to learn Japanese in a short period of time, there is no other school (that you should consider) but this one.
examples.japanese: 日本語を短期間で習得したいのならこの学校をおいてほかに(は)ない。

examples.english: No other director has been involved with as many works as Mr. Y.
examples.japanese: これほど多くの作品を手がけた監督はY氏をおいてほかにいない。

examples.english: There is no one to save you but yourself.
examples.japanese: あなたを救うのはあなた自身をおいてほかにない。

examples.english: There is no company in Japan but ours that can provide this level of professionalism and rich experience.
examples.japanese: これほどのプロフェッショナリズムと豊かな経験を提供できる会社は、日本中で当社をおいてほかにはありません。

examples.english: I cannot think of another country that is as indifferent to contracts as this one is.
examples.japanese: 契約に対してこれだけ無神経な国はこの国をおいてほかに思いつかない。

examples.english: We cannot think of anyone who can handle this role but Jane.
examples.japanese: この役割をこなせるのはジェーンをおいてほかに考えられない。

examples.english: The only peaches that satisfy the two requirements of good taste and beautiful shape are the ones from Yamanashi Prefecture. (literally: No peaches satisfy the two requirements, i.e., good taste and a beautiful shape, but those from Yamanashi Prefecture.)
examples.japanese: 味のよさと形の美しさ、この二つの要件を満たす桃は、山梨県産をおいてほかにない。

examples.english: There is no language but English that is used as widely for communication among non-native speakers.
examples.japanese: 非母国語話者の間のコミュニケーションにおいてこれほど広範囲に用いられている言語は、英語をおいてほかには存在しない。

points.explanation: をおいてほかに（は）～ない A phrase that means "there is nothing else besides X".
points.meaning: (there is) no ~ but X; X is the only one; nothing else is ~ but X; no other ~ are/do something as ~ as X

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

| リサをおいてほかに(は)いない | There is no one else but Lisa |
variants: をおいてほかに（は）～ない
