examples.english: When you come up to Tokyo, please be sure to stop by.
examples.japanese: 上京の折(に)はぜひお立ち寄り下さい。

examples.english: When I returned to Japan last time, I met with my high school friends.
examples.japanese: この前日本に帰った折(に)高校時代の友達に会った。

examples.english: If you need any help, please contact me sooner rather than later.
examples.japanese: 援助が必要な折(に)は早めに連絡して下さい。

examples.english: When you are in the area, please use our shop.
examples.japanese: 近くにお越しの折には、ぜひ当店をご利用下さい。

examples.english: When I was on business in L.A., I stopped by my son's university dormitory to see how he was doing.
examples.japanese: ロスへ出張した折に息子の様子を見るために大学の寮に寄ってみた。

examples.english: When I went into downtown Tokyo, I also went (literally: extended my trip) to the used book store district.
examples.japanese: 都心に出た折に、古本屋街に足を延ばした。

examples.english: If you have a suit like this, you don't have to worry what to wear for (literally: on the occasions of) weddings and funeral services.
examples.japanese: こういうスーツを持っていれば冠婚葬祭の折に着るものを心配しなくてもいい。

examples.english: I lost the watch my parents bought for me for my graduation.
examples.japanese: 卒業の折に親に買ってもらった時計をなくしてしまった。

examples.english: I was saddled with debt and didn't know what to do. On that occasion, there was a call from him.
examples.japanese: 私は大きな借金をかかえて途方にくれていました。そんな折に彼から電話があったのです。

points.explanation: 折(に) A noun indicating special/uncommon and primarily desirable occasions which someone takes advantage of, or where someone is expected to do something or where something desirable takes place.
points.meaning: On the occasion; at the time; when; if; opportunity; chance

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Nounの | 折(に) | |
| 休暇の折(に) | On vacation |
(ii) Vinformal | 折(に) | |
| 京都へ{行く/行った}折(に) | When I go/went to Kyoto |
(iii) Adjectiveいinformal nonpast | 折(に) | |
| 寒さの厳しい折(に) | At a time when it is severely cold |
(iv) Adjectiveなstemな | 折(に) | |
| 暇な折(に) | When you have leisure time |
(v) Demonstrative adjective | 折(に) | |
| その折(に) | On that occasion; at that time |

examples.english: Due to the typhoon (literally: the typhoon's inﬂuence), there is a chance of heavy rain across Western Japan.
examples.japanese: 台風の影響で、西日本は大雨の恐れがある。

examples.english: This war could become a second Vietnam War. (literally: There is a risk that this war will become a second Vietnam War.)
examples.japanese: この戦争は第二のベトナム戦争になる恐れがある。

examples.english: There is concern that terrorists have entered the country.
examples.japanese: テロリストたちが入国した恐れがある。

examples.english: We are worried that the measurement errors may be large.
examples.japanese: 測定誤差が大きい恐れがある。

examples.english: The tumour may be malignant.
examples.japanese: 腫瘍が悪性である恐れがある。

examples.english: The wild animals in this region are in danger of becoming extinct.
examples.japanese: この地域の野性動物は絶滅の恐れがある。

examples.english: Company M announced that there is a risk that some of their cell phone models may generate heat.
examples.japanese: M社は自社の携帯電話のいくつかの機種に発熱の恐れがあると発表した。

examples.english: This chemical can cause blindness (literally: when it gets in an eye), so please wear protective goggles.
examples.japanese: この薬品が目に入ると失明の恐れがあるので、保護眼鏡を着用して下さい。

examples.english: The prefectural government will soon begin an investigation of the ground conﬁguration, land use, etc. in places where there is some fear of landslides.
examples.japanese: 県は近く、がけ崩れなどの恐れがある場所で地形や土地利用状況などの調査を始める。

examples.english: If you open attached ﬁles without paying close attention, you risk infecting (your computer) with a virus.
examples.japanese: 添付書類を不用意に開けるとウイルスに感染する恐れがある。

examples.english: This drug is said to have no side effects, but if you take it for more than eight weeks straight, there is a risk that it will damage your liver.
examples.japanese: この薬は副作用がないと言われているが、８週間以上続けて服用すると肝臓に害を及ぼす恐れがある。

examples.english: We're concerned that the players are still practicing, not knowing that the game has been cancelled.
examples.japanese: 選手たちが試合の中止を知らないまま、まだ練習している恐れがある。

examples.english: The Metropolitan Police Ofﬁce announced that there is some concern that murder suspect A has escaped overseas.
examples.japanese: 警視庁は、殺人容疑者のAが海外へ逃亡した恐れがあると発表した。

examples.english: The ingredients used (in the food) at this cafeteria may be old.
examples.japanese: ここのカフェテリアは食材が古い恐れがある。

examples.english: This drug may be harmful to embryos.
examples.japanese: この薬は胎児に有害である恐れがある。

examples.english: We're worried that we may be dealing with a (Japanese) maﬁa group.
examples.japanese: 取引相手が暴力団である恐れがある。

points.explanation: A phrase that means "it is feared (that)""
points.meaning: It is feared (that); we fear (that); we are worried/concerned (that); there is a fear/risk/chance/concern/etc.; can; could; may; it is possible (that); be in danger of

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Nounの | 恐れがある | |
| 洪水の恐れがある | There is a fear of flood |
| 爆発の恐れがある | There is a fear of an explosion |
(ii) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | 恐れがある | |
| {傷つける/傷つけた}恐れがある | There is a fear that someone/something will hurt/has hurt someone/something |
| (品物が){古い/古かった}恐れがある | There is a fear that something is/was old |
(iii) Adjectiveなstem | {な/である/だった/であった}恐れがある | "Adjectiveなstemな" is rarely used |
| 不安定{な/である/だった/であった}恐れがある | There is a fear that something is/was unstable |
(iv) Noun{である/だった/であった} | 恐れがある | |
| 不良品{である/だった/であった}恐れがある | There is a fear that something is/was a defective product |

examples.english: This company will employ you regardless of your educational background if you have (relevant work) experience.
examples.japanese: この会社は、経験があれば学歴を問わず採用してくれる。

examples.english: You have to have an individual consultation with your homeroom teacher whether you work or go on to college after graduation.
examples.japanese: 卒業後就職するか進学するかを問わず、担任との個人面談を受けなければならない。

examples.english: Copying this software is (an) illegal (act) whether or not it is a complete copy.
examples.japanese: 本ソフトウエアの複製は全部か否かを問わず違法行為になる。

examples.english: We'll buy the electrical appliances which you are not using whether they are new or used.
examples.japanese: 不要の電化製品、中古新品を問わず買い取ります。

examples.english: At this church we offer wedding ceremonies for everyone, regardless of whether or not you are Christian (literally: a believer).
examples.japanese: 当教会は、信者であるなしを問わず挙式をお引き受けいたします。

examples.english: Anyone can join this club whether or not they have experience/regardless of their experience (literally: whether he/she has experience or not).
examples.japanese: 経験のあるなしを問わず誰でもこのクラブに参加できます。

examples.english: Company A is beginning their marketing in Japan without considering the results of their market research.
examples.japanese: A社は、市場調査の結果のいかんを問わず、日本でのマーケティングを開始する。

examples.english: In order to use university facilities, no matter what the purpose (literally: what kind of use), you need approval from the university beforehand.
examples.japanese: どうような利用であるかを問わず学内の施設利用は事前に大学の承認が必要だ。

examples.english: Mountain climbing, hiking, skiing, etc., can be enjoyed at this resort area, regardless of the season.
examples.japanese: このリゾート地は、登山、ハイキング、スキー等、四季を問わず一年中楽しめる。

examples.english: Thanks to wireless LAN, now we can access the network wherever and whenever we need it.
examples.japanese: 無線ランのおかげで、場所や時間を問わずネットへのアクセスが可能になった。

examples.english: We buy old personal computers regardless of the manufacturer.
examples.japanese: 古くなったパソコン、メーカーを問わず引き取ります。

examples.english: This is one book you should definitely read, whether or not you are interested in the Muslim world.
examples.japanese: この本は、イスラム世界に興味があるか否かを問わず、ぜひ読んでおくべき一冊である。

examples.english: Using the campus facilities, including computers and bulletin boards, for election campaigning or other similar activities is prohibited whether it is during an election period or not.
examples.japanese: 選挙期間中であるか否かを問わず、選挙運動またはこれに類する行為にコンピュータ、掲示板等学内施設を利用することを禁ずる。

examples.english: Instructors Wanted (Men or Women) [Advertisement]
examples.japanese: インストラクター募集。(男女をを問わず)

examples.english: I recommend that you get this DVD whether you have seen the (original) movie or not.
examples.japanese: このDVDは映画を見た見ないを問わず、ぜひ持っておくことを勧めます。

examples.english: Anyone can use this software easily whether he/she is familiar with personal computers or not.
examples.japanese: このソフトはパソコンに精通しているいないを問わず、誰でも簡単に使える。

points.explanation: A compound particle that means "without questioning".
points.meaning: Regardless of; irrespective of; without reference to; whether X or Y; whether X or not; whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun1({、/ と/や}Noun2) | を問わず | |
| 年齢を問わず | Regardless of age |
| 年齢、性別を問わず | Regardless of age and sex |
| 年齢と性別を問わず | Regardless of age and sex |
| 年齢や性別を問わず | Regardless of age, sex, etc. |
(ii) XかYか | を問わず | Where X,Y=contrastive words; usually nonpast forms |
Noun1かNoun2か | 男性か女性かを問わず | Whether someone is a male or a female |
V1かV2informalか | 去るか留まるかを問わず | Whether someone leaves or stays |
Adjectiveい1informalかAdjectiveい2informalか | 暑いか寒いかを問わず | Whether it is hot or cold |
Adjectiveな1stemかAdjectiveな2stemか | 便利か不便かを問わず | Whether something is convenient or inconvenient |
(iii) Xか{どう/否}か | を問わず | |
| 行くか{どう/否}かを問わず | Whether someone goes or not |
| 高いか{どう/否}かを問わず | Whether something is expensive or not |
| 便利(である)か{どう/否}かを問わず | Whether something is convenient or not |
| 日本人か{どう/否}かを問わず | Whether someone is Japanese or not |
(iv) X(affirmative)+X(negative) | を問わず | |
| 行く行かないを問わず | Whether someone goes or not |
| うまいうまくないを問わず | Whether someone is skillful or not |
| 上手、上手じゃないを問わず | Whether someone is skillful or not |
| 日本人、日本人じゃないを問わず | Whether someone is Japanese or not |
(v) X+Y | を問わず | Where X, Y=Adjectiveいinformal nonpast/Adjectiveなstem; Y=X’s antonym |
| 高い安いを問わず | Whether something is expensive or cheap |
| 上手下手を問わず | Whether someone is skillful or unskillful |
(vi) {Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | であるなしを問わず | |
| 会員であるなしを問わず | Whether someone is a member or not |
| 経済的であるなしを問わず | Whether something is economical or not |
(vii) Nounのあるなし | を問わず | |
| 経験のあるなしを問わず | Whether someone has experience or not |
(viii) Nounのいかん | を問わず | |
| 方法のいかんを問わず | Regardless of the method |
(ix) Wh-sentence informalか | を問わず | |
| いかなる国における使用であるかを問わず | In whatever country something may be used |

examples.english: The computer models and software we used are listed in Table 1.
examples.japanese: 使用した機種及びソフトウエアを表１に示す。

examples.english: The qualifications for applying for this scholarship require (literally: are) that you be a Japanese citizen and a student at a four-year college in this country.
examples.japanese: 本奨学金への応募資格は、日本国籍を有すること、及び国内の四年制大学に在籍する学生であることである。

examples.english: Smoking in the rooms and halls is prohibited.
examples.japanese: 室内及び廊下での喫煙は禁止されています。

examples.english: In this month's issue we introduce sightseeing spots in Hiroshima and neighbouring prefectures.
examples.japanese: 今月号では広島及び近郊他県の観光名所を紹介します。

examples.english: We hereby notify you of the relocation of the head office and the change of our company name.
examples.japanese: 本店移転及び商号変更についてお知らせいたします。

examples.english: Company A announced that it would no longer offer technical support for products made before 2003 (literally: in and before 2002).
examples.japanese: A社は２００２年及びそれ以前の製品のサポートの打ち切りを発表した。

examples.english: This is a report on the status of the discharge and treatment of general waste nationwide last year.
examples.japanese: これは昨年度における全国の一般廃棄物の排出及び処理状況に関する報告である。

examples.english: Before holding a press conference it is necessary to make sure that the information is accurate and that it can be (literally: it is information which can be) released to the public.
examples.japanese: 記者会見の前に、情報が正確であること、及びそれが公表してもいい情報であることを確認しておく必要がある。

examples.english: We have conﬁrmed that there is no signiﬁcant damage to the device, and that it has been maintained according to the regulations.
examples.japanese: 装置には著しい破損のないこと、及びメンテナンスが規定どおり行われていることを確認した。

examples.english: It is now required that the body for evaluating companies that accept foreign interns have a committee of (literally: which consists of) ﬁve or more members, and that the majority of the committee members have (literally: be those who have) professional expertise regarding internships for foreigners.
examples.japanese: 外国人研修生を受け入れる事業者の評価機関は、5人以上の委員からなる委員会を持つこと、及びその委員の半数以上が外国人の研修について専門知識を持つことが義務づけられた。

points.explanation: A particle that connects two nouns or noun phrases.
points.meaning: And

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Noun1 | 及びNoun2 | |
| 名古屋及びその周辺 | Nagoya and the surrounding areas |
(ii) Sentence1 informalこと、 | 及びSentence2 informalこと | だ cannot be used before こと. Adjectiveなstem {な/である}こと; Nounであること |
| 情報を収集すること、及びそれを分析すること | Collecting information and analysing it |
| 好き{な/である}こと、及び上手{な/である}こと | Liking something and excelling at something |
| 教師であること、及び父親であること | Being a teacher and being a father |

examples.english: I'm convinced that I've watched all the movies that are commonly considered masterpieces.
examples.japanese: 私はおよそ名作と言われている映画はすべて見ているつもりだ。

examples.english: She is not at all suited for work that requires perseverance like this work does.
examples.japanese: 彼女はこういう根気のいる仕事にはおよそ向いていない。

examples.english: I can make a fairly good guess about what he's thinking.
examples.japanese: 彼の考えていることはおよそ想像がつく。

examples.english: That academic association has approximately 1,500 members.
examples.japanese: その学会にはおよそ１５００人の会員がいる。

examples.english: Generally, none of the skills you can learn easily will become second nature.
examples.japanese: およそ楽をして得られる技能で身につくものはない。

examples.english: Generally, anyone who is called a genius carries a heavy burden others can't see.
examples.japanese: およそ天才と言われる人は誰でも人には知れない重荷を背負っているものだ。

examples.english: We've been bound by this utterly irrational system for a long time.
examples.japanese: 我々はおよそ不合理なこの制度に長い間縛られている。

examples.english: Professor Tamiya was totally removed from university politics.
examples.japanese: 田宮先生は大学の政治的なことにはおよそ縁遠い人だった。

examples.english: I'm sorry for him, but his effort was totally meaningless.
examples.japanese: 彼には気の毒だが、彼の努力はおよそ意味のないものだった。

examples.english: It was behaviour we couldn't even have imagined based on what he usually said and did.
examples.japanese: それは彼の普段の言動からはおよそ想像できない行動であった。

examples.english: I ﬁnished most of my work this morning, so it looks like I can go home early today.
examples.japanese: 仕事は午前中でおよそ片づいたので今日は早く帰れそうだ。

examples.english: Most of the information on that university can be obtained via the Internet.
examples.japanese: その大学のおよその情報はインターネットで得られる。

examples.english: Approximately what is the volume of this company's annual business?
examples.japanese: この会社の年間取引額はおよそどのくらいですか。

examples.english: They say there are about 1,000 giant pandas living in China now.
examples.japanese: 現在中国に生息するジャイアントパンダの数はおよそ１千頭ということだ。

points.explanation: An adverb representing the ideas "all; totally; mostly; approximately".
points.meaning: Generally; commonly; all; quite entirely; totally; utterly; (not) at all; for the most part; mostly; almost; approximately; roughly; about; rough; general

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) およそ | Nounは | Where Adjective(い/な) has a negative meaning |
| およそ優れた研究者は | excellent researchers in general; all excellent researchers |
(ii) およそ | Adjective(い/な) | |
| およそつまらない | Quite boring |
| およそ不可能だ | Totally impossible |
(iii) およそ | {Vnegative/Adjectiveいstemく/Adjectiveなstemで}ない | |
| およそ向いていない | Someone is not at all suited for something |
| およそ面白くない | Something is not at all interesting |
| およそ経済的でない | Something is not economical at all |
(iv) およそ | {V/Adjective(い/な}/Nounだ} | |
| およそ分かる | Someone understands almost everything |
| およそ正しい | Something/someone is about right |
| およそ完成だ | Something is almost complete |
(v) およそ | のNoun | |
| およそ考え | A general idea |
| およそ見積もり | A rough estimate |
(vi) およそ | Number(+Counter) | |
| およそ十万人 | Approximately 100,000 people |

examples.english: Setting aside people's criticism, the prime minister declared his support for the Iraq War.
examples.japanese: 首相は国民の批判をよそにイラク戦争支持を表明した。

examples.english: During my adolescent years, I secluded myself at home and read science ﬁction, ignoring my friends, who were spending all their time dating.
examples.japanese: 青春時代、友達がデートに明け暮れるのをよそに、僕は家に一人こもってSFを読んでいた。

examples.english: Despite our worries, many people participated in the event, so it turned out to be a big success.
examples.japanese: 今回のイベントは、我々の心配をよそに多くの参加者を集め、大成功だった。

examples.english: Ignoring his wife's repeated advice, he never quit drinking and smoking.
examples.japanese: たび重なる妻の忠告をよそに、彼は酒もタバコもやめなかった。

examples.english: Feeling that it would be his last chance for love, he ignored the warnings of those around him, and allowed himself to get deeply involved.
examples.japanese: 彼はその恋を自身の最後の恋と感じて、周囲の警告をよそにのめり込んでいった。

examples.english: In December 2006, the revision of the Fundamental Law of Education was passed without sufﬁcient deliberation by the Diet, despite opposition from various sectors.
examples.japanese: ２００６年12月、様々な反対の声をよそに、教育基本法改正案が国会の十分な審議を経ることなく可決された。

examples.english: Despite the heartfelt pleas of peace-minded citizens who want to abolish all nuclear weapons, the nuclear arms race and the development of nuclear weapons still know no limits.
examples.japanese: 平和を希求する市民による核兵器廃絶への切なる願いをよそに、核兵器開発、核軍拡競争は、今なおとどまるところを知りません。

examples.english: Contrary to the many countries in the world that enthusiastically pursue economic growth, this country is pursuing happiness based on an afﬂuent life for individuals.
examples.japanese: 多くの国々が経済発展ばかりに躍起になっているのをよそに、この国は個人の豊かな生活を基盤にした幸福を追求している。

points.explanation: A compound particle that expresses someone’s indifference to warnings, criticism, advice, accusations, opposition, anxiety, wishes, eagerness, provocative actions, etc.
points.meaning: Indifferent to ~; contrary to ~; ignoring ~; despite

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) NP | をよそに | |
| 不景気をよそに | Indifferent to economic recession |
(ii) Sinformalの | をよそに | だ cannot be used before の. Adjectiveなstem{な/である}の;Nounであるの |
| 困っているのをよそに | Indifferent to the fact that someone is having trouble |
| 不便{な/である}のをよそに | Ignoring the inconvenience |
| 不況であるのをよそに | Indifferent to the state of depression |

examples.english: Koji drank the cold coffee with a look that showed how bad it tasted.
examples.japanese: 浩二は冷めたコーヒーをさもまずそうに飲んだ。

examples.english: Furuta talks as if he suffered alone, but the truth of the matter is that he just complained and didn't do any work.
examples.japanese: 古田はさも自分一人が苦労したように言っているが、実は彼は文句を言うばかりで何もしなかったのだ。

examples.english: Let's take him to the hospital right now. If we don't, it's going to be too late.
examples.japanese: 今すぐ病院に連れて行こう。さもないと手遅れになる。

examples.english: The person in charge listened to my complaint with an expression that revealed it was truly bothersome.
examples.japanese: 係員はさも面倒くさそうに私の苦情を聞いていた。

examples.english: She acts as if she were truly busy, but really she doesn't have anything signiﬁcant to work on.
examples.japanese: 彼女はさも忙しそうにしているが、本当は大した仕事なんかないのだ。

examples.english: The children are listening to the lecture looking really bored.
examples.japanese: 子供たちはさも退屈そうな顔をして授業を聞いている。

examples.english: Kawamura always tells that story as if it were his own experience, but actually I told it to him.
examples.japanese: 川村はいつもその話をさも自分自身の体験みたいに話しているが、本当はそれは私が彼に話したことなのだ。

examples.english: The division chief ordered me to come to the ofﬁce on Sunday as if it were a matter of course.
examples.japanese: 部長はさも当然のごとく私に日曜出勤を命じた。

examples.english: When I read the operation manual, it sounds like the program is really easy to use, but I wonder if that's really true.
examples.japanese: そのプログラムは、操作説明書を見るとさも簡単に使えそうに書いてあるが、本当にそうなのだろうか。

examples.english: The man approached me as if he knew me very well.
examples.japanese: 男はさも親しげに私に近寄ってきた。

examples.english: Toda's way of talking (literally: That way Toda has of talking), as if he knew everything about wine, is truly offensive.
examples.japanese: あの「自分はさもワインの通ですよ」って感じの戸田の話し方はまったく嫌みだ。

points.explanation: An adverb meaning "truly," used when describing the way someone’s action or behaviour appears.
points.meaning: Truly; really; as if; so; that way; like that

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) さも | {Adjective(い/な)stem/Vます}そう{に/な} | |
| さも嬉しそうに | Looking really happy; as if someone were happy |
| さも嬉しそうな顔 | A face that shows someone is truly happy; the face of someone who is truly happy |
| さも不自由そうに | As if someone really had trouble moving |
| さも不自由そう歩き方 | A way of walking that shows someone really has trouble walking; a walk that looks as if someone has trouble moving easily |
| さも誰にでもできそうに | As if anyone could do (it) |
| さも誰にでもできそうな説明 | Instructions that sound as if anyone could do (it) |
(ii) さも～ | {V/Adjectiveい}informalよう{に/な} | |
| さも自分ができるように | As if someone were capable |
| さも自分ができるような話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were capable |
| さも自分が偉いように | As if someone were great |
| さも自分が偉いような話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were great |
(iii) さも～ | Adjectiveなstem{な/だった}よう{に/な} | |
| さも自分が上手なように | As if someone were good at something |
| さも自分が上手なような話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were good at something |
(iv) さも～ | Noun{の/だった}よう{に/な} | |
| さも自分が専門家のように | As if someone were an expert |
| さも自分が専門家のような話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were an expert |
(v) さも～ | {V/Adjectiveい}informalみたい{に/な} | |
| さも自分ができるみたいに | As if someone were capable |
| さも自分ができるみたいな話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were capable |
| さも自分が偉いみたいに | As if someone were great |
| さも自分が偉いみたいな話し方 | A way of talking that sounds as if someone were great |
(vi) さも～ | {Adjectiveなstem/Noun}{∅/だった}みたい{に/な} | |
| さも自分が上手みたいに | As if someone were good at something |

examples.english: An even larger hurricane struck South Texas.
examples.japanese: 更に大きいハリケーンがテキサス南部を襲った。

examples.english: The last translation (job) was difficult, but this one is even harder.
examples.japanese: 前の翻訳も難しかったが今度のは更に難しい。

examples.english: In our global age, we must promote the internationalization of businesses even more forcefully.
examples.japanese: グローバル時代に向けて企業の国際化を更に強力に押し進める必要がある。

examples.english: It is expected that an additional 500 employees will be laid off.
examples.japanese: 更に５００人の人員が整理される見通しだ。

examples.english: It looks like our nation's economy will worsen still further.
examples.japanese: 我が国の経済は更に悪化しそうだ。

examples.english: It has been decided that an even larger jumbo jet will be developed.
examples.japanese: 更に大型のジャンボジェットが開発されることになった。

examples.english: Company D's laptop computers have become even thinner.
examples.japanese: D社のノート型コンピュータが更に薄くなった。

examples.english: We provide electrical appliances even more cheaply than discount shops do.
examples.japanese: 電化製品をディスカウントショップより更にお安く提供しております。

examples.english: The price of the memory was lowered by an additional 10 percent.
examples.japanese: メモリが更に10パーセント値下げされた。

examples.english: More mergers took place among major banks this year.
examples.japanese: 今年は主要銀行の合併が更に進んだ。

examples.english: There is fear that the damage caused by bird ﬂu will spread even further.
examples.japanese: 鳥インフルエンザの被害が更に広がる恐れがある。

examples.english: Data is collected with a sensor and, furthermore, on the same chip the data is augmented with an ampliﬁer.
examples.japanese: センサーでデータを集め、これを更に同一チップ上の増幅器で増幅する。

examples.english: We'll give a commemorative souvenir to all customers on opening day. In addition, we'll give a gift certiﬁcate for our store to 50 people selected in a drawing.
examples.japanese: 開店日の来場者にはもれなく記念品を差し上げます。更に、抽選で50名の方に当店の商品券が当たります。

examples.english: Well, I should be going now.
examples.japanese: さて、私はそろそろ失礼します。

examples.english: Now, on another matter, Japan is undergoing quite a Korea boom at this time.
examples.japanese: さて、話は変わりますが、日本では今ちょっとした韓国ブームです。

examples.english: Now I'm going to talk about the main topic.
examples.japanese: さて、それでは本題に入りましょう。

examples.english: Now, let's review the points I have discussed so far.
examples.japanese: さて、ここで今までお話ししたポイントを復習してみましょう。

examples.english: The World Cup has begun! So, which country's going to win this time?
examples.japanese: ワールドカップ開幕！さて、今回はどこが勝つでしょうか。

examples.english: Well, what shall we do now (literally: from now)?
examples.japanese: さて、これからどうしようか。

examples.english: Now, (I'd like to talk) about the contract change I requested the other day. Did you have a chance to discuss it within your department?
examples.japanese: さて、先日お願いしました契約変更の件ですが、課内部でご検討いただけましたでしょうか。

examples.english: Now, I'm going to continue where we left off in the previous lecture. Do you remember (what we covered before)?
examples.japanese: さて、前回の講義の続きですが、覚えていますか。

examples.english: Now, let's turn to sports. [TV/radio news]
examples.japanese: さて、次はスポーツです。

examples.english: Here are three portraits. So, which one is Ms. Yoshinaga?
examples.japanese: ここに3枚のポートレートがあります。さて、吉永さんはどれでしょう。

examples.english: Well, I guess I'll go to bed now.
examples.japanese: さて、もう寝ようかな。

examples.english: Well, I'm in trouble.
examples.japanese: さて、困った。

examples.english: So, what shall we begin with?
examples.japanese: さて、何から始めようか。

points.explanation: An interjection indicating that the speaker/writer is going to talk about something different.
points.meaning: Well; now; well now; so

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

examples.english: I imagine the people in the disaster-stricken areas are having a really hard time.
examples.japanese: 被災地の人々はさぞかし困っているだろうと思う。

examples.english: Moving to Aomori (for a new assignment) without your family must be very tough.
examples.japanese: 青森への単身赴任はさぞ(かし)大変でしょう。

examples.english: I'm sure winter in Chicago will be very cold.
examples.japanese: シカゴの冬はさぞ(かし)寒いに違いない。

examples.english: I forgot her birthday, so I'm sure Alice is really mad.
examples.japanese: 誕生日を忘れてしまったんだから、アリスはさぞ怒っているだろう。

examples.english: She must have been so happy after hearing the news that she'd been accepted (to college)!
examples.japanese: 彼女は大学合格の知らせを聞いてさぞ喜んだだろう。

examples.english: I imagine Professor Tanimoto is quite tired after her long trip.
examples.japanese: 谷本先生は長旅でさぞかしお疲れだろうと思います。

examples.english: Christmas is almost here. I'm sure children are really looking forward to it.
examples.japanese: もうすぐクリスマス。子供たちはさぞ楽しみなことでしょう。

examples.english: Takashi didn't hear that sound, so he must have been sleeping very heavily.
examples.japanese: 孝史はあの音が聞こえなかったのだから、さぞかしよく寝ていたに違いない。

examples.english: He's already talking about what happens after they win, so he must be really conﬁdent.
examples.japanese: 彼はもう勝った後のことを話しているから、さぞかし自信があるんだろうね。

examples.english: To begin with, I cannot agree with our way of judging where we point out only the ﬂaws of a piece and never mention the good points.
examples.japanese: 私はそもそも、作品のいいところをコメントしないで欠点ばかり指摘する審査のやり方に賛成できない。

examples.english: The problem is that they built a supermarket in a place like this to begin with.
examples.japanese: そもそもこんなところにスーパーを造ったことが問題だ。

examples.english: How was such a ridiculous plan approved in the ﬁrst place?
examples.japanese: そもそもどうしてこんなばかばかしい企画が通ったのでしょうか。

examples.english: This whole incident started when an employee took one of the ofﬁce computers home. (literally: The very origin of this incident was in the fact that an employee took one of the ofﬁce computers home.)
examples.japanese: 今回の事件のそもそもの起こりは、一人の社員が会社のパソコンをうちに持ち帰ったことにあった。

examples.english: To begin with, humans are not solitary beings.
examples.japanese: そもそも人間は一人で生きているのではない。

examples.english: To begin with, why on earth are you at this party?

examples.english: That we were hoping for great things from him was our ﬁrst mistake.
examples.japanese: 彼に期待したことがそもそもの間違いだった。

examples.english: The fundamental problem was that there was a mistranslation in the contract.
examples.japanese: 契約書に誤訳があったのがそもそもの問題だ。

examples.english: If you remain a negative thinker, your life itself will be ruined.
examples.japanese: マイナス思考ばかりしていると、人生そのものが駄目になる。

examples.english: The plan itself is not bad.
examples.japanese: 企画そのものは悪くない。

examples.english: This country is the perfect deﬁnition of an autocracy.
examples.japanese: この国は独裁国家そのものだ。

examples.english: I think that obscene images themselves are not the problem; who sees them is the problem.
examples.japanese: わいせつ画像は、それそのものが問題なのではなく、それを誰が見るかが問題だと思う。

examples.english: Mr. Takeda is 80 this year and the picture of health.
examples.japanese: 武田さんは今年８０歳だが、健康そのものだ。

examples.english: I doubt this group's very existence.
examples.japanese: 私はこの団体の存在そのものを疑っている。

examples.english: Not only do we want to reform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but we hope the current diplomacy itself will change.
examples.japanese: 我々は外務省改革にとどまらず、現在の外交そのものの転換を望む。

examples.english: The epitome of a person is his or her thinking. (literally: A human being is his or her thought itself.)
examples.japanese: 人間はその人の考えそのものである。

examples.english: For me, volleyball was life itself.
examples.japanese: 私にとってバレーボールは人生そのものでした。

examples.english: The land itself does not produce wealth, but wealth is produced when people conduct economic activities, such as production and sales, on it (literally: by (people's) conducting economic activities such as production and sales on it).
examples.japanese: 土地は、それそのものは富を生み出さないが、その上で生産、販売などの経済活動を行うことで富を生み出す。

examples.english: (literally: Their way of) Aiming at the elderly and forcing them to sign a house repair contract is utterly contemptible.
examples.japanese: お年寄りを狙い、強引な方法で家屋の修理契約を結ぶ手口は卑劣そのものだ。

examples.english: The manual's explanations and figures are perfectly clear, so even people with no knowledge of image processing will be able to understand them well.
examples.japanese: そのマニュアルは説明も図も明快そのもので、画像処理の知識がない者にもよく分かる。

examples.english: Ms. Yonekura is known for his totally sincere personality.
examples.japanese: 米倉さんは誠実そのものの人柄で知られている。

examples.english: You can make a big proﬁt when you invest in the right stocks, but the risk (of loss) is just as big.
examples.japanese: 株式投資は当たった時の利益は大きいが、それだけリスクも大きい。

examples.english: This job is hard work, but to the same extent I also ﬁnd it rewarding.
examples.japanese: この仕事は苦労も多いが、それだけやりがいもある。

examples.english: It might be that they hate each other that much more because they are in different sects of the same religion.
examples.japanese: 彼らは同じ宗教内の派閥だから、それだけ憎しみも大きいのかもしれない。

examples.english: If your expectations are high, your disappointment will be equally high.
examples.japanese: 期待が大きいとそれだけ失望も大きくなってしまう。

examples.english: That he was assigned a big job just shows what high hopes people have for him.
examples.japanese: 大きな仕事をまかされたということは、それだけ期待されているということだろう。

examples.english: It is good to have many options, but it means that it's that much harder to choose.
examples.japanese: たくさんのオプションがあるのはいいのだが、それだけ選択に悩むことにもなる。

examples.english: It's not true of pollen allergy drugs that the sleepier they make you, the more effective they are.
examples.japanese: 花粉症の薬は、眠くなるからそれだけ効くというわけではありません。

examples.english: If you specify as many conditions as you can, your search should turn up someone that is much closer to your ideal.
examples.japanese: できるだけ多く条件を指定すると、それだけ理想に近い人が検索されるはずです。

examples.english: If information from two sources is consistent, don't you think the information is that much more reliable?
examples.japanese: 情報の内容が二つのソースで一致するのなら、それだけ信用できるということではないだろうか。

examples.english: It seems that it's a common, and mistaken, assumption that the amount of money you spend on your children equals the amount of affection you've given them.
examples.japanese: 子供にお金をかければそれだけ愛情を注いだことになる、という間違った思い込みがしばしばあるようだ。

examples.english: The fact that we have been getting more letters from readers recently about this problem shows how much more it is drawing people's attention.
examples.japanese: これに関する読者からの投書が最近増えているということは、それだけこの問題が注目されてきたということでしょう。

examples.english: (Compared with those who are less experienced,) Sales representatives with a lot of experience should be all the more able to win their customers' trust.
examples.japanese: 販売経験が豊富な営業マンは、それだけ顧客の信頼も多く勝ち取るはずだ。

points.explanation: An adverbial phrase indicating that the degree of something is proportionate to the degree of the state, action or event mentioned in the preceding sentence.

examples.english: I think people who are called geniuses suffer in their own way.
examples.japanese: 天才と言われる人にはそれなりの苦しみがあると思う。

examples.english: If you (really) listen to classical music, jazz and rock, each of them is interesting in its own way.
examples.japanese: クラシックもジャズもロックも、聞いてみればみなそれなりに面白い。

examples.english: Working abroad is interesting, but you must expect a certain amount of hardship, too.
examples.japanese: 外国で仕事をするのは面白いが、それなりの苦労は覚悟しなければならない。

examples.english: All the reference books I have bought have been helpful in their own way.
examples.japanese: 買った参考書はどれもみなそれなりに役に立っている。

examples.english: All the players are giving it their best in their own way. We just haven't had the (expected) result.
examples.japanese: 選手たちはみんなそれなりに精一杯やっている。ただ結果が出ないだけだ。

examples.english: Even if you don't have money, there are ways to enjoy your leisure in your own way.
examples.japanese: お金がなくてもそれなりに余暇を楽しむ方法はある。

examples.english: I think that even though most people have worries and problems, they are living the best they can (literally: in their own ways).
examples.japanese: ほとんどの人は、悩みや問題があってもそれなりに暮らしているのだと思います。

examples.english: If you are in a high-ranking position, you have to assume the responsibilities that come with it.
examples.japanese: 上の地位にいればそれなりの責任がかかってくる。

examples.english: For a tough assignment we should pay appropriate compensation.
examples.japanese: きつい仕事にはそれなりの報酬を払うべきだ。

examples.english: If I can achieve the expected performance this year, it looks like I'll be promoted to branch manager next year.
examples.japanese: 今年それなりの成績を上げることができれば、来年支店長に昇進できそうだ。

examples.english: If you have a reasonable income, you should be able to ﬁnd someone to marry soon.
examples.japanese: それなりの収入があるのなら、結婚相手はすぐ見つかるはずです。

examples.english: The fact that he made it to the semiﬁnals means that he had the right skills to take him that far.
examples.japanese: 彼が準決勝まで残ったということは、それなりの実力があるということだ。

examples.english: There's a reason no one likes her (literally: she is not liked by everyone).
examples.japanese: 彼女がみんなに好かれていないのはそれなりの理由がある。

examples.english: I think people who are called geniuses suffer in their own way.
examples.japanese: 天才と言われる人にはそれなりの苦しみがあると思う。

examples.english: If you (really) listen to classical music, jazz and rock, each of them is interesting in its own way.
examples.japanese: クラシックもジャズもロックも、聞いてみればみなそれなりに面白い。

examples.english: Working abroad is interesting, but you must expect a certain amount of hardship, too.
examples.japanese: 外国で仕事をするのは面白いが、それなりの苦労は覚悟しなければならない。

examples.english: All the reference books I have bought have been helpful in their own way.
examples.japanese: 買った参考書はどれもみなそれなりに役に立っている。

examples.english: All the players are giving it their best in their own way. We just haven't had the (expected) result.
examples.japanese: 選手たちはみんなそれなりに精一杯やっている。ただ結果が出ないだけだ。

examples.english: Even if you don't have money, there are ways to enjoy your leisure in your own way.
examples.japanese: お金がなくてもそれなりに余暇を楽しむ方法はある。

examples.english: I think that even though most people have worries and problems, they are living the best they can (literally: in their own ways).
examples.japanese: ほとんどの人は、悩みや問題があってもそれなりに暮らしているのだと思います。

examples.english: If you are in a high-ranking position, you have to assume the responsibilities that come with it.
examples.japanese: 上の地位にいればそれなりの責任がかかってくる。

examples.english: For a tough assignment we should pay appropriate compensation.
examples.japanese: きつい仕事にはそれなりの報酬を払うべきだ。

examples.english: If I can achieve the expected performance this year, it looks like I'll be promoted to branch manager next year.
examples.japanese: 今年それなりの成績を上げることができれば、来年支店長に昇進できそうだ。

examples.english: If you have a reasonable income, you should be able to ﬁnd someone to marry soon.
examples.japanese: それなりの収入があるのなら、結婚相手はすぐ見つかるはずです。

examples.english: The fact that he made it to the semiﬁnals means that he had the right skills to take him that far.
examples.japanese: 彼が準決勝まで残ったということは、それなりの実力があるということだ。

examples.english: There's a reason no one likes her (literally: she is not liked by everyone).
examples.japanese: 彼女がみんなに好かれていないのはそれなりの理由がある。

points.explanation: それなりに・の A phrase representing the idea that someone/something does something or is in a state in his/her/its own way, or in a way suitable to the situation or generally expected from the situation.
points.meaning: In one’s own way; accompanying; proportionate; suitable; expected; agreeable; reasonable; one’s own; proper to

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) それなりに | {V/Adjective(い/な)/Noun+Copula} | |
| それなりに楽しめる | Something can be enjoyed in its own way |
| それなりに美味しい | Something is tasty in its own way |
| それなりに便利だ | Something is convenient in its own way |
| それなりに傑作だ | Something is an excellent work in its own way |
(ii) それなりの | Noun | |
| それなりの利点 | Merits proper to something |

examples.english: After much hesitation, I decided to give my friends a set of coffee cups as a wedding present.
examples.japanese: さんざん迷った末に、友達の結婚祝いはコーヒーカップのセットを贈ることにした。

examples.english: After much trial and error, we ﬁnally made a fuel cell battery that can be used in cars.
examples.japanese: 試行錯誤の末(に)、やっと車に使える燃料電池ができた。

examples.english: After considering it for a week, I decided to leave my family behind and transfer to my new job alone.
examples.japanese: 一週間悩んだ末(に)、家族をおいて単身赴任することにした。

examples.english: After eight hours of negotiation, both parties ﬁnally came to an agreement.
examples.japanese: 両者は8時間にわたる交渉の末に、ついに合意に達した。

examples.english: After a close game lasting more than ﬁve hours, the Tigers won.
examples.japanese: 5時間を超える熱戦の末、タイガースが勝った。

examples.english: After more than a year of difﬁcult merger negotiations, M Bank and U Bank ﬁnally came to an agreement.
examples.japanese: M銀行とU銀行の合併交渉は１年以上も難航した末、やっと成立した。

examples.english: After almost twenty bad sketches, I finally managed to draw one I liked.
examples.japanese: 下書きを20枚近く失敗した末に、やっとなんとか気に入った絵ができた。

examples.english: After much trouble looking for a new job, I found one with an IT-related company that valued my previous computer experience.
examples.japanese: 再就職は、苦労した末、過去のコンピュータ経験を評価してくれたIT関係の会社に決まりました。

examples.english: The man tried to run away and, in the end, he was arrested after resisting violently.
examples.japanese: 男は走って逃げ、最後には暴れ回って抵抗した末に逮捕された。

examples.english: This plan was a product of compromise, reached after working through a clash of opinions between the countries.
examples.japanese: この案は、各国の意見が衝突した末の「妥協の産物」だった。

points.explanation: 末（に）A noun that indicates the end of a period or the time after long, hard mental or physical work.
points.meaning: After; at the end of

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Nounの | 末(に) | |
| 今月の末(に) | At the end of this month |
| 交渉の末(に) | After negotiation |
(ii) Vinformal past | 末(に) | |
| よく考えた末(に) | After thinking hard |

examples.english: I think just showing up for a while will be enough.
examples.japanese: ちょっと顔を見せるだけで済むと思う。

examples.english: The interview took only 20 minutes.
examples.japanese: 面接は20分で済んだ。

examples.english: Because the Japanese (in it) was not very difﬁcult, I managed (to read it) without a dictionary.
examples.japanese: あまり難しい日本語ではなかったので、辞書なしで済んだ。

examples.english: Everywhere I travelled I was able to use my credit card, so I could travel without cash.
examples.japanese: 旅行先ではどこでもクレジットカードが使えたので、現金がなくても済んだ。

examples.english: This is not the kind of problem where you can get away with staying silent.
examples.japanese: これは黙っていて済む問題ではない。

examples.english: I've been given a scholarship, so I think I can get by without borrowing money.
examples.japanese: 奨学金をもらったので、お金を借り{ずに/なくて(も)/ないで}済むと思う。

examples.english: When you want to cancel the agreement, all you will lose is the enrolment fee.
examples.japanese: 解約したい時は、入会金だけ損をすれば済む。

examples.english: Three days should be enough for a translation like this.
examples.japanese: この程度の翻訳なら3日で済むだろう。

examples.english: Because this approach would allow us to use most of the current system, our new investment will be minimal (literally: we could get by with a minimal investment).
examples.japanese: この方法だと今のシステムの大部分がそのまま使えるので、新たな投資が最小で済む。

examples.english: Aren't you being wasteful by driving places where you could walk or go by bicycle?
examples.japanese: 徒歩あるいは自転車で済むところへ車で行く無駄をしていませんか。

examples.english: It was 15 km/hr above (the speed limit), but fortunately I got off with just a warning.
examples.japanese: 15キロオーバーだったが、幸い警告だけで済んだ。

examples.english: You can't excuse a major mistake like this just by saying, ""Sorry,"" or ""I didn't know.""
examples.japanese: こんな大きな失敗をして「ごめん」「知らなかった」では済まない。

examples.english: Because electric bicycles are not powered solely by motor, the law classiﬁes them as bicycles, so you can ride them without either a driver's license or a helmet.
examples.japanese: 電動自転車はモーターの力だけで動くことはないから、法律上「自転車」とされ、運転免許もヘルメットもなしで済む。

examples.english: From here we can go anywhere by subway, so we don't need a car.
examples.japanese: ここからは地下鉄でどこへでも行けるから車がなくても済む。

examples.english: Sometimes an apology is not enough. (literally: There are things that can be settled by apologizing and things that cannot.)
examples.japanese: 謝って済むことと済まないことがある。

examples.english: Because I was wearing a helmet, I suffered only minor injuries.
examples.japanese: ヘルメットをかぶっていたので、怪我が軽くて済んだ。

points.explanation: A verb that means "to be finished; to do (in the sense of being enough)".
points.meaning: Take/cost/need/etc. only ~; do/manage (without/only with); get by/get away (without/only with); be let off (without/only with); be enough (if); be all right (if); not to have to: there is no need for

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Number(+Counter)で | 済む | |
| ２０ドルで済む | Something costs only 20 dollars |
(ii) Noun {(だけ)/なし}で | 済む | |
| 電話(だけ)で済む | (just) a telephone call is enough |
| 検査なしで済む | Not have to have/give an examination; do without an exam |
(iii) Nounがなくても | 済む | |
| 携帯電話がなくても済む | Manage without a cell phone |
(iv) {Vて/Adjectiveいstem} | くて済む | |
| 謝って済む | Get away with just apologising |
| 安くて済む | Something costs only a little |
(v) Vinformalだけで | 済む | |
| 行くだけで済む | Just going is enough; get by with just going |
(vi) Vnegative {ずに/なくて(も)/ないで} | 済む | Exception: する→せずに |
| 行か{ずに/なくて(も)/ないで}済む | Do not have to go; be all right if someone doesn’t go |
(vii) {Vconditionalば/Vinformal past}ら | 済む | |
| {借りれば/借りたら}済む | Be all right if someone borrows something |

examples.english: This area is close to both the station and a supermarket, so it's convenient, but the environment is not very good.
examples.japanese: この辺りは駅にもスーパーにも近くて便利だ。ただ環境があまりよくない。

examples.english: I think this is a very good computer. But, the price is a problem.
examples.japanese: とてもいいコンピュータだと思います。ただ値段が問題ですね。

examples.english: He is a nice person, only I'm concerned that he is a little shallow.
examples.japanese: 彼はいい人だ{が/けど}、ただちょっと考えが浅いところが気になる。

examples.english: It's not impossible to repair this problem, only I think it'll take time.
examples.japanese: この故障は直せないことはないと思います。ただ時間がかかると思います。

examples.english: It is a very quiet and nice house, only there are no shops nearby, so it's inconvenient for shopping.
examples.japanese: とても静かでいいうちだ。ただ近くに店がないので買い物は不便だ。

examples.english: This digital camera has many outstanding functions. However, the problem is that it's hard to use because the user interface is bad.
examples.japanese: このデジカメ優れた機能をたくさん持っている。ただユーザーインターフェースが悪くて使いにくいのが難点だ。

examples.english: For most things, if I'm not available others can do it for me; however, as far as this job is concerned, I cannot ask someone else to do it for me.
examples.japanese: たいていのことは私がいなくても他の者が代わりにやってくれるが、ただこの仕事は他の者に頼むわけにはいかない。

points.explanation: A conjunction that introduces a supplementary remark.
points.meaning: But; however; only; the only thing is that ~

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) ただ | One+Counter (のNoun) | |
| ただ一人の息子 | The only son |
| ただ一発で | With only one shot |
(ii) ただ | One+CounterもVerbal(negative) | |
| ただ一日も休んだことがない | Have not taken even one day off |
(iii) ただ | Nounだけ(Particle) | |
| Nounだけ(Particle) 単語だけ(を)覚える | Remember only words |
| Nounだけ(Particle) 力だけで解決する | Solve something only with force |
(iv) ただ | Verbal(という)だけ(だ) | |
| ただ読んだ(という)だけ(だ) | Someone just read it; that’s all |
| ただ安い(という)だけ(だ) | Something is just cheap; that’s all |
| ただ{静かな/静かだという}だけ(だ) | Something is just quiet; that’s all |
| ただ大学教授(だ)(という)だけ(だ) | Someone is just a college professor; that’s all |

examples.english: You may look at any of the magazines or books in this room. However, please do not take them out of the room.
examples.japanese: この部屋にある雑誌や本はどれを見てもいいです。但し、部屋からは持ち出さないで下さい。

examples.english: This hall is open from 9 a.m. to 6 pm. However, for special events, the hall is not limited to these hours.
examples.japanese: 当館の開館時間は午前9時から午後６時まで。但し、特別行事がある場合はこの限りではない。

examples.english: You may consult dictionaries' during the exam. However, (you may use) only Japanese-English dictionaries.
examples.japanese: 試験の時、辞書を見てもいいです。但し、和英辞典だけです。

examples.english: We sell this product at 30 percent off the list price. But we cannot accept returns.
examples.japanese: この製品は定価の3割引きで販売しています。但し、返品はできません。

examples.english: Please (feel free to) talk to me whenever you have a problem. However, I cannot help you with money matters.
examples.japanese: 問題があったらいつでも相談して下さい。但し、お金の問題は相談に乗れません。

examples.english: You can choose any topic for your presentation. However, the presentation should be 20 minutes or fewer.
examples.japanese: 発表のトピックは何でもかまいません。但し、発表時間は20分以内です。

examples.english: The hours of the internship are from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. However, there will be a break from 12:00 to 1:00.
examples.japanese: 実習時間は午前8時30分から午後5時30分まで。但し、12時から1時までは休憩時間とする。

examples.english: Decisions at the general meeting are passed by a majority of the members. However this does not apply to revisions of the regulations.
examples.japanese: 総会の議決は会員の過半数を以って決定される。但し、規定改定はこの限りではない。

examples.english: Article 7 (Routes of business trips, etc.): As a rule, for business travel, choose routes and means of transportation with economy in mind (literally: placing the most importance on economy). However, there can be exceptions when there is a special reason.
examples.japanese: 第７条(出張の経路等)出張の経路とその利用交通機関は、経済性を重視して選ぶことを原則とする。但し、特別の理由がある場合はこの限りではない。

examples.english: V=IR where V is the potential difference between Points A and B, I is the electric current, and R is the resistance.
examples.japanese: V＝IR但し、VはAB間の電位差、Iは電流、Rは抵抗

points.explanation: 但し・ただしA conjunction indicating that there is a condition, restriction, proviso, etc., to the preceding statement.
points.meaning: However; but; only; here; provided that

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure: Sentence1。 | 但し、Sentence。 |

examples.english: It's just something a child told you. You don't have to take it so seriously.
examples.japanese: たかが子供の言ったことだ。そんなに深刻に考えることはない。

examples.english: You shouldn't make light of it saying it's just a cartoon.
examples.japanese: たかが漫画(くらい)と馬鹿にしてはいけない。

examples.english: You don't need to make such a big fuss over a little car trouble.
examples.japanese: たかが車の故障(くらい)でそんなに大騒ぎする必要はない。

examples.english: You don't have to get so mad at me just for borrowing your bicycle without asking.
examples.japanese: たかが無断で自転車を借りたくらい(のこと)でそんなに怒らなくてもいいでしょう。

examples.english: One person's wisdom doesn't amount to much.
examples.japanese: 人間一人の知恵などたかが知れている。

examples.english: It's only smoking. Why do they have to talk about us as if we were criminals?
examples.japanese: たかが喫煙じゃないか。どうしてそんなに犯罪者のように言われなきゃならないんだ。

examples.english: You may say it's just a notebook, but to me it's very important.
examples.japanese: たかがノートくらいと言われるかもしれませんが、僕にとってはとても大事なものなんです。

examples.english: What do you expect us to do with only 100,000 yen?
examples.japanese: たかが１０万円で何ができると言うのですか。

examples.english: I don't want to bother you with just apartment hunting.
examples.japanese: たかがアパート探しくらいで君に面倒をかけたくない。

examples.english: It is overreacting to call an ambulance just for falling down.
examples.japanese: たかが転んだくらいで救急車を呼ぶなんて大げさだ。

examples.english: There's hardly any area in which the economy can be improved through public projects.
examples.japanese: 公共事業によって景気が回復する領域などたかが知れている。

examples.english: It's just (a matter of) a chair. But it can affect your productivity at work and inﬂuence your health.
examples.japanese: たかが椅子。しかし、これによって仕事の能率が大きく左右されるし健康にも影響する。

examples.english: It's just a cold, but it is a cold.
examples.japanese: たかが風邪、されど風邪。

points.explanation: A noun modiﬁer used when the speaker thinks little of the referent of the modiﬁed noun or noun phrase.
points.meaning: Only; just; mere

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) たかが | Nounだ | |
| たかが子供だ | Someone is only a child |
(ii) たかが | {Noun/Number(+Counter)} (くらい){と/で} | |
| たかがレポート(くらい)と | Thinking/saying that it’s only a report |
| たかがレポート(くらい)で | Over just a report |
| たかが二人(くらい)と | Thinking/saying that (there are only) two people |
| たかが二人(くらい)で | With just two people |
(iii) たかが～ | {V/Adjectiveい}informal くらい (のこと)で | |
| たかが英語が{できる/できた}くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone can/could speak English; just for (things like) being able to speak English |
| たかが成績{悪い/悪かった}くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone’s performance is/was poor; just for (things like) someone’s poor performance |
(iv) たかが～ | Adjectiveなstem{な/だった} くらい (のこと)で | |
| たかが料理が下手{な/だった} くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone is/was bad a cooking; just for (something like) being a poor cook |

examples.english: He sat in the chair and stayed there, silent the whole time.
examples.japanese: 彼は椅子に腰掛けたなり(で)、ずっと黙っていた。

examples.english: I was told to close my eyes for a few seconds while I kept lifting one foot off the ground.
examples.japanese: 片足を上げたなりの格好で、数秒間目をつぶるように言われた。

examples.english: Junichi went to France when he was 17 and never came back to Japan; he became a painter and now has settled in Montmartre.
examples.japanese: 純一は17歳の時にフランスに行ったなりで、日本には帰らず画家になって、今ではモンマルトルに住みついている。

examples.english: Elisa bought The Tale of Genji, but she left it on the bookshelf without reading a single page.
examples.japanese: エリサは『源氏物語』を買ったなり、一ページも読まず、本棚に置きっぱなしだった。

examples.english: My sweetheart stood at the entrance to my room, grinning.
examples.japanese: 彼は私の部屋の入り口に突っ立ったなりでニヤニヤ笑っていた。

examples.english: My wife opened the door for me, but I had fallen down and couldn't move an inch.
examples.japanese: 妻がドアを開けてくれたんですけど、私はもう倒れたなりで、体が動きませんでした。

examples.english: Because I was sitting for a long time with my lower back twisted, it hurt so much I couldn't stand up.
examples.japanese: 腰をよじったなりの姿勢で長時間座っていたので、立てないほど腰が痛くなった。

examples.english: The doll sits on a shelf, covered with dust.
examples.japanese: 人形がほこりをかぶったなりで棚に乗っかっている。

examples.english: You can withdraw money from this ATM in multiples of 1,000 yen.
examples.japanese: このATMは千円単位でお金を引き出すことができる。

examples.english: This in-house investigation will examine the recycling rate for each section.
examples.japanese: この社内調査では課単位でリサイクル実施率を調べる。

examples.english: In Japan, tea cups are often sold in sets of ﬁve.
examples.japanese: 日本では湯飲みは5個単位で売られることが多い。

examples.english: If our company's plan to send labourers from Asia is successful this time, next time we will greatly expand the scale and send labourers in groups of 1,000.
examples.japanese: 我が社は今回のアジアからの労働者派遣が成功した場合には、次回から規模を大幅に拡大し、千人単位で派遣する予定だ。

examples.english: B Company's new data communication service allows the user to transmit and receive data in one-minute units for a minimum contract amount of 150 hours.
examples.japanese: B社の新しいデータ通信サービスは、最低契約量である１５０時間分のデータ通信を１分単位で利用できる。

examples.english: They say the online bookstore Z is going to sell books by the page or the chapter.
examples.japanese: オンライン書店のZ社は、本をページまたは章単位で販売するそうだ。

examples.english: This new version of the project management software application allows us to plan and manage (our operations) by the hour and minute, instead of the day.
examples.japanese: このプロジェクト管理ソフトの新バージョンでは、これまで日単位で行われていた計画と管理を時間・分単位で行えるようになった。

points.explanation: A phrase that indicates the smallest amount, number or unit of something (or people) involved.
points.meaning: By the; in sets/groups/lots/etc. of; in multiples of; each; every

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:

| 十人単位で | In groups of ten |

examples.english: This is simply a matter/problem of cultural differences.
examples.japanese: これは単に文化の違いの問題だ。

examples.english: They did nothing more to this car than change the body design.
examples.japanese: この車は単にボディーのデザインを変えただけだ。

examples.english: It's not that the job is difficult; it's simply that I'm clumsy.
examples.japanese: 仕事が難しいのではなく、単に私が不器用なだけです。

examples.english: The effects of the high yen are not limited to exports.
examples.japanese: 円高の影響は単に輸出だけにとどまらない。

examples.english: This is nothing more than my personal opinion.
examples.japanese: これは単に私個人の意見に過ぎない。

examples.english: It's simply an issue of interpretation.
examples.japanese: それは単に解釈の問題だ。

examples.english: This is not just a problem for you alone.
examples.japanese: これは単にあなた一人の問題ではない。

examples.english: This text is simply something that was translated literally from the original.
examples.japanese: この文章は単に原文を直訳しただけだ。

examples.english: Our hotel is not simply inexpensive; with our comprehensive array of services, you can stay (with us) in comfort.
examples.japanese: 当ホテルは単に安いだけでなく、行き届いたサービスで快適にお過ごしいただけます。

examples.english: Today, a company that simply racks up large proﬁts cannot be called a ﬁrst-class company.
examples.japanese: 今は単に多くの利益を上げているだけでは一流企業とは言えない。

examples.english: With this camera you can take high quality pictures just by holding it toward an object and clicking the shutter.
examples.japanese: このカメラは、単に被写体にカメラを向けてシャッターを押すだけで高画質の写真を撮ることができる。

examples.english: He is not consistent in his thinking; he's simply stubborn.
examples.japanese: 彼は考えが一貫しているのではなく、単に頑固なだけだ。

examples.english: Germany is no more than my birthplace (literally: It is simply that my birthplace is Germany), so I know nothing about Germany, let alone German.
examples.japanese: 私は単に生まれがドイツだっただけで、ドイツ語はもちろんドイツのことは何も知らない。

examples.english: It's not that Masao is poor only at math.
examples.japanese: 雅夫は単に数学だけができないのではない。

examples.english: In this case, it's wrong to blame only Agnes.
examples.japanese: この場合、単にアグネスだけを非難するのは間違っている。

examples.english: It's nothing more than your speculation.
examples.japanese: それは単に君の憶測に過ぎない。

examples.english: There are creatures in this lake that exist only here; in fact, there are more than 50 species.
examples.japanese: この湖にはここにしかいないという生物がおり、その数たるや50種類を超える。

examples.english: How do they ever choose (who wins) the Nobel Prize in Literature? (I think) The number of works of literature published around the world in a year must be enormous.
examples.japanese: ノーベル文学賞はどうやって選考するのだろう。1年間に世界で発表される文学作品の数たるや膨大なものだと思うのだが。

examples.english: In the spring of 1987, he ﬁnally made his debut. But, the result of that ﬁrst match was so miserable.
examples.japanese: １９８７年春、彼はついにデビューを果たした。しかし、その初戦の結果たるや散々なものだった。

examples.english: His banjo playing is the best. Particularly when it comes to his fast plucking technique, I can't imagine anyone in the world who could do it better.
examples.japanese: 彼のバンジョーは最高だ。特にその速弾きテクニックたるやたぶん世界でも彼の右に出る者はいないのではないだろうか。

examples.english: The fee for joining this diet class is certainly not cheap, but the results are tremendous!
examples.japanese: このダイエット教室の参加費は決して安くはないが、その効果たるや絶大である。

examples.english: RoboCup is a competition where soccer-playing robots compete to be ﬁrst in the world. Since the ﬁrst championship was held in Nagoya in 1997, an international competition has been held every year, and the ""players'"" skills have shown remarkable improvement since the first tournament.
examples.japanese: ロボカップは、サッカーをするロボットの世界一を競う大会である。１９９７年に名古屋で第1回大会が開かれて以来、国際大会が毎年開かれてきたが、その間の「選手」の技量の向上たるや著しい。

points.explanation: A compound particle used to present a subtopic about which the writer provides surprising or impressive information.
points.meaning: When it comes to ~; speaking of

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

examples.english: It's not fun traveling (literally: if I travel) alone.
examples.japanese: 一人で旅行に行ったって面白くない。

examples.english: I make it a rule to buy good quality things even if they are a little more expensive.
examples.japanese: 私は少しくらい高く(っ)たって、質のいいものを買うことにしている。

examples.english: No matter how good someone's Japanese is, he/she cannot do this translation without technical knowledge (in this ﬁeld).
examples.japanese: いくら日本語が上手だって専門知識がなかったらこの翻訳はできないよ。

examples.english: Even professionals make mistakes. (literally: Even if he is a professional, there are times when he makes a mistake.)
examples.japanese: プロだって失敗することもある。

examples.english: Even if you change your job, it won't solve the problem.
examples.japanese: 仕事を変えたって問題は解決しない。

examples.english: Even if it's a struggle, you shouldn't give up.
examples.japanese: 苦しくったって諦めちゃいけない。

examples.english: Whether it's old or new, a good thing is good.
examples.japanese: 古くたって新しくたって、よいものはよいのだ。

examples.english: No matter how convenient (the location) is for commuting, the rent is too high.
examples.japanese: いくら通勤に便利だってこの家賃は高すぎる。

examples.english: No matter who it is, anyone would get mad if you said that to him.
examples.japanese: 誰だってそんなことを言われたら腹が立つよ。

examples.english: You can do this job even if you don't have a computer.
examples.japanese: コンピュータがなくったってこの仕事はできる。

examples.english: Even if you don't cook yourself, you can easily get what you want to eat now if you just pay for it.
examples.japanese: 自分で料理しなくたって、お金さえ出せば食べたいものが簡単に手に入るようになった。

examples.english: You'll never be able to do it alone! (literally: Even if you try to do it alone, that's impossible.)
examples.japanese: 一人でしよう(っ)たって、それは無理だ。

examples.english: Even if you wanted to go buy it right now, the stores are all already closed.
examples.japanese: 今すぐ買いに行く(っ)たって、もう店はみんな閉まっている。

examples.english: Even though it's said to be expensive, my guess is it won't cost more than one million yen.
examples.japanese: 高い(っ)たって、１００万円はしないだろう。

examples.english: Although she has experience teaching Japanese, she hasn't yet taught anywhere outside of Japan.
examples.japanese: 日本語教育の経験者(だ)ったって、彼女はまだ日本以外で教えたことはない。

examples.english: That house is not something you could buy even if you wanted to.
examples.japanese: あの家は君が買おうったって買えるようなものじゃない。

examples.english: It won't work if you try to cheat me.
examples.japanese: 僕を騙そうったってそうはいかない。

examples.english: Whatever he may want to say, I don't think I'll stop it.
examples.japanese: 彼が何を言おうったってそれをとめようとは思わない。

examples.english: There are no more trains even if (you say) you want to go home now.
examples.japanese: 今から帰るったってもう電車はないよ。

examples.english: Even if you say you'll look through the materials, it's impossible for you to do it alone because there are so many.
examples.japanese: 調べるったって、こんなたくさんある資料を一人で調べるのは無理だ。

examples.english: Although (I say) it's close, it's not a distance you can walk at all.
examples.japanese: 近いったってとても歩いて行ける距離じゃない。

examples.english: No matter how simple (they say) it is, in fact you won't be able to use it without a minimum knowledge of computers.
examples.japanese: いくら簡単ったって、やっぱり最低限のパソコン知識がなくては使えない。

examples.english: Although I say ""fasting,"" it's not like you can't put anything in your mouth. You can drink vegetable juice twice a day.
examples.japanese: 「断食」ったって、全く何も口に入れないんじゃない。1日に2回、野菜ジュースを飲むことはできる。

examples.english: We just cannot be content with our past performance.
examples.japanese: 過去の業績に安住してばかりはいられない。

examples.english: Indeed, this is a serious situation, but we cannot just keep discussing it.
examples.japanese: 確かにこれは深刻な事態だが、議論ばかりしてはいられない。

examples.english: Just because the people around me have helped me out in the past, I can't depend on others endlessly.
examples.japanese: 周りの人が助けてくれるからと言って、いつまでも人にばかり頼ってはいられない。

examples.english: I ﬁnally own a house, which I have hoped to do for years, but I can't remain excited for long. Now I have a huge loan to repay.
examples.japanese: やっと長年の夢であったマイホーム手に入れたが、喜んでばかりはいられない。これから大きなローンを返していかなければならないのだ。

examples.english: I haven't fully recovered from the shock of being laid off (literally: the restructuring shock), but I cannot waste my time just feeling depressed. I have to start looking for a job right away.
examples.japanese: リストラのショックからまだ完全に立ち直ったわけじゃないけど、いつまでも落ち込んでばかりもいられない。すぐに仕事探しを始めなければ。

examples.english: I just can't let it get me down because I didn't get into the school I wanted.
examples.japanese: 希望の学校に入れなかったからと言って、くじけてばかりはいられない。

examples.english: We can't just sit around being impressed by someone else's success. We have to work harder, too.
examples.japanese: 人の成功に感心ばかりしてはいられない。我々ももっと頑張らなければ。

examples.english: We can't just keep thinking about what caused the trouble. We have to recover the lost data immediately.
examples.japanese: 障害の原因ばかり考えてもいられない。早急に失われたデータを回復する必要がある。

examples.english: Now that I'm retired I can live as I like, but I just can't stay at home, so I've begun to do volunteer work.
examples.japanese: 退職して悠々自適の生活ができるようになったが、家にばかりこもってもいられないのでボランティアの仕事を始めた。
