examples.english: If (it is true that) you look up unfamiliar words in the dictionary every time you encounter a new one, you will never learn to read fast.
examples.japanese: 知らない単語が出てくるたびに辞書を引いているようではいつまでたっても速く読めない。

examples.english: If (it is true that) apartments in Tokyo are that expensive, we cannot live there.
examples.japanese: アパートがそんなに高いようでは私たちは東京には住めない。

examples.english: If you continue to show the level of performance you have to date, we will have a problem. (literally: If your performance is like what you have exhibited up to now, it's a problem.)
examples.japanese: 成績が今までのようでは困ります。

examples.english: If you complain like that now, it will be difﬁcult to complete this job.
examples.japanese: 今からそんなに文句を言っているようでは、この仕事をやり遂げるのは難しいだろう。

examples.english: If (it is true that) he doesn't help you when you are in trouble, you cannot call him a friend.
examples.japanese: 困った時に助けてくれないようでは友達とは言えない。

examples.english: If it is true that) you have trouble getting up early in the morning (literally: are weak in the morning), you probably won't be able to do this job.
examples.japanese: 朝が弱いようではこの仕事は無理でしょう。

examples.english: It is a problem if (it is true that) it takes four or ﬁve forms to request a travel reimbursement for an amount as small as one thousand yen.
examples.japanese: 千円程度の旅費払い戻しに4枚も5枚も書類が必要なようでは問題だ。

examples.english: If you're doing things like that now, there's no way you'll meet the deadline.
examples.japanese: 今頃そんなことをしているようでは、とても締め切りに間に合わない。

examples.english: If (it is true that) you cannot take care of the people under you, you are not qualiﬁed to be their boss.
examples.japanese: 部下の面倒が見られないようでは上司失格だ。

examples.english: Even if we make an effort to increase research funding, with the university facilities the way they are (literally: if the university facilities are in their present condition), we won't be able to utilize the funds effectively.
examples.japanese: 大学の施設が現状のようでは、せっかく研究資金を増やしても有効に活用できない。

examples.english: If we play the next game like (we did in) today's game, there's no way we can advance to the ﬁnals.
examples.japanese: 次の試合も今日の試合のようでは、とても決勝には進めない。

points.explanation: A conjunction that presents an undesirable situation, which is assumed to be factual.
points.meaning: If; if it is true that; if it is the case that

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

examples.english: Mr. Yamano is very strict about time; if you happen to be even five minutes late for an appointment with him, he won't meet with you again.
examples.japanese: 山野氏は非常に時間に厳しい人で、面会時間に5分も遅れようものなら以後二度と会ってはもらえない。

examples.english: I'm particularly sensitive to cigarette smoke, so when someone is smoking nearby, I cannot concentrate on anything.
examples.japanese: 私はタバコの煙に特に敏感で、近くで吸われようものならもう何事にも集中できなくなってしまう。

examples.english: In New York, if you happen to take even a second to move (your car) forward after the trafﬁc light turns green, the driver behind you honks at you immediately.
examples.japanese: ニューヨークでは信号が青に変わって一秒でも発進が遅れようものなら、すかさず後ろからクラクションを鳴らされる。

examples.english: On this island, you can have fun walking and swimming in the ocean on sunny days, but if it happens to rain, there's nothing to do.
examples.japanese: この島は、晴れていれば散歩や海水浴などが楽しめるが、雨に降られようものなら何もやることがなくなる。

examples.english: The seats in this airplane have an extremely small amount of space between them, so if someone in the seat ahead chooses to lean back, large people like me are stuck (literally: are in a situation in which they literally cannot move).
examples.japanese: この飛行機は前の座席との間隔が極端に狭いので、私のように大きい人間は、前の人に椅子を倒されようものなら、文字通り身動きできなくなってしまう。

examples.english: The frequent visits of door-to-door salesmen these days are a real headache. The salesmen won't leave even if you say ""no thanks,"" and if you happen to let them in the house by mistake, they won't leave until you buy (their products).
examples.japanese: 最近頻繁にやってくる訪問販売は頭痛の種です。断っても簡単には帰りませんし、うっかり家の中に入れようものなら買うまで帰りません。

examples.english: If you happen to go out on a motorcycle in pollen season (literally: pollen allergy season) by mistake, you'll keep sneezing and be miserable inside your full-face helmet.
examples.japanese: 花粉症の季節にうっかりバイクで出かけようものなら、走行中にくしゃみ連発でフルフェイスのヘルメットの中は悲惨な状態になる。

examples.english: This ﬁsh is very poisonous, and if you happen to be stung, that area will swell a lot.
examples.japanese: この魚は猛毒を持っていて、間違ってそのトゲに刺されようものなら、患部が大きく腫れ上がってしまう。

examples.english: Ms. Tamura has taken up (studying) Chinese medicine recently and if you ask her about it by mistake, you will end up listening to (her talk about) its effects for a full hour.
examples.japanese: 田村さんは最近漢方医学に凝っていて、うっかりそのことを聞こうものなら、たっぷり一時間はその効用を聞くはめになる。

points.explanation: A conjunctive phrase that presents an undesirable hypothetical situation.
points.meaning: If ~ happen to; if ~ at all; if ~ choose to

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:

| 聞こうものなら | If someone asks at all |

examples.english: Even though I want to contact Toru, I don't know either her phone number or her e-mail address.
examples.japanese: 徹に連絡しようにも電話番号もメールアドレスも知らない。

examples.english: I have a terrible headache, and I cannot get up even though I want to.
examples.japanese: ひどく頭が痛くて起きようにも起きられない。

examples.english: Even though I'm thinking of writing an article, I have nothing to write about.
examples.japanese: 記事を書こうにも書く材料がない。

examples.english: Although I wanted to complain, I didn't know who to complain to.
examples.japanese: 苦情を言おうにも誰に言っていいか分からなかった。

examples.english: Although I'm trying to move my body, every part aches and I can't even lift my arms.
examples.japanese: 体を動かそうにもあちこち痛くて腕も上げられない。

examples.english: It's sad that even though she wants to talk to someone about her troubles, she has no one to talk to near her.
examples.japanese: 気の毒に彼女は悩み事を相談しようにも相談できる人が近くにいない。

examples.english: Although I am thinking of going for counselling, the variation in quality and schools of thought makes me sceptical.
examples.japanese: カウンセリングに行こうにも、その質や学派も様々でついつい懐疑的になってしまいます。

examples.english: Although I wanted to buy the book, it was out of print.
examples.japanese: その本は買おうにも絶版だった。

examples.english: Because my cell phone battery is dead, I cannot make a call even though I want to.
examples.japanese: 携帯電話の電池が切れたので、電話をかけようにもかけられない。

points.explanation: ようにも（～ない） A conjunctive phrase that indicates concession: "even though someone tries to do something, he/she cannot do it for some reason".

examples.english: I heard of your promotion this time to manager of the headquarters' sales department. Please accept my sincere congratulations.
examples.japanese: この度は本社営業部長にご栄転の由、誠におめでとう存じます。

examples.english: It is said that an international conference on global environmental protection will be held in this city next year.
examples.japanese: 地球環境保護の国際会議が来年当市で開催される由(である)。

examples.english: I've been informed that next year Professor Nozawa is going to Germany for a year.
examples.japanese: 野沢先生は来年一年ドイツにいらっしゃる由、伺っております。

examples.english: I heard that you gave birth to your ﬁrst child and I send my heartfelt congratulations.
examples.japanese: 第一子御出産の由、心からお祝い申し上げます。

examples.english: We learned that your stay at our hotel was not a pleasant one. We are very sorry for that.
examples.japanese: 当ホテルでのご滞在が快適でなかった由、誠に申し訳なく存じます。

examples.english: I heard about the trafﬁc accident. I am relieved to hear that you were not hurt.
examples.japanese: 交通事故のこと伺いました。お怪我などなかった由、ほっといたしております。

examples.english: I was informed that there was not much damage on Ishigaki Island because, luckily, the typhoon missed it (literally: swerved away from it).

examples.japanese: 日本消費者連盟は、一部ウイスキーの不正表示に関して、公正取引委員会に申し入れる由である。

examples.english: I heard from Mr. Yoshimoto that you will be attending the reception.
examples.japanese: 懇親会にご出席の由、吉本君から連絡を受けました。

examples.english: We learned that your stay at our hotel was not a pleasant one. We are very sorry for that.

examples.english: Whatever (other) people say, I believe my child.
examples.japanese: 人が何と言おう{と/が}、私は自分の子供を信じている。

examples.english: Even if people say I'm stubborn or stupid, I'll do what I believe.
examples.japanese: 頑固と言われよう{と/が}馬鹿と言われよう{と/が}、私は自分の信じることをやります。

examples.english: That professor keeps lecturing (literally: advances his lecture) regardless of whether his students understand it or not.
examples.japanese: あの教授は学生が分かろう{と/が}分かるまい{と/が}、かまわず授業を進めていく。

examples.english: It doesn't matter whether his English is good or bad.
examples.japanese: 英語が上手だろう{と/が}下手だろう{と/が}そういうことは関係ない。

examples.english: We'll adopt anything good, whether it's a work by a professional or an amateur.
examples.japanese: プロの作品だろう{と/が}素人の作品だろう{と/が}いいものは採用する。

examples.english: Whatever I do, it's none of your business.
examples.japanese: 人が何をしようと大きなお世話だ。

examples.english: We don't care how much it may cost. We have to win this lawsuit by any means.
examples.japanese: 費用がいくらかかろうとかまわない。何としてもこの訴訟勝たなければならない。

examples.english: He is saying bad things about his boss without regard to whether or not others are listening.
examples.japanese: 彼はみんなが聞いていようがおかまいなしで、上司の悪口を言っている。

examples.english: Even if their children are running around or spilling drinks, the parents are too caught up in their own conversation to scold them.
examples.japanese: 自分の子供たちが走り回ろうが飲み物をこぼそうが、親たちは叱りもしないで自分たちの話に夢中になっている。

examples.english: Whether she's going to marry or not, it has nothing to do with me.
examples.japanese: 彼女が結婚しようがするまいが、そんなことは私には関係ないことだ。

examples.english: Whether it's expensive or cheap, we should buy it if we need it.
examples.japanese: 高かろうが安かろうが、必要なものなら買えばいい。

examples.english: We're going ahead with the tour as scheduled even if we have only one participant.
examples.japanese: 参加者がたとえ一人であろうとツアーは予定通り行います。

examples.english: It doesn't matter whether she is Japanese or American. If I fall in love (with someone), I'll marry that person.
examples.japanese: 日本人だろうがアメリカ人だろうが、そういうことは関係ない。好きになったら結婚する。

examples.english: Because of her good looks, she also has many things to worry about.
examples.japanese: 彼女はその美貌(の)故(に)、悩みも多い。

examples.english: Because you want the end result to be perfect, you end up being distracted by little things.
examples.japanese: 結果にこだわりすぎる(が)故(に)、小さなことに心を奪われることになる。

examples.english: This is an extremely delicate problem; therefore, we must handle it very carefully.
examples.japanese: これは極めてデリケートな問題だ。(それ(が)/その)故に、慎重に取り組む必要がある。

examples.english: His mind was strengthened because of his serious illness.
examples.japanese: 彼の精神は大病の故に強靭になった。

examples.english: Electronic texts are easy to revise and present to the public, but because of these characteristics, it is difﬁcult to trace publicly-displayed electronic texts back to their original data.
examples.japanese: 電子テキストは改変と公開が容易であるが、この特徴故に公開されている電子テキストは元データを追跡することが難しい。

examples.english: Because cell phones are convenient, we have to be careful not to use them incorrectly.
examples.japanese: 携帯電話は便利故に、使い方を誤らないようにしなければならない。

examples.english: Mountains are not sacred just because they are tall.
examples.japanese: 山は高いが故に尊からず。

examples.english: Because the Japanese archipelago extends north and south, the temperature difference (within Japan) is great.
examples.japanese: 日本列島は南北に伸びているが故に、温度差が大きい。

examples.english: In the United States even now there are cases in which someone is discriminated against because he or she is black.
examples.japanese: アメリカでは今でも黒人であるが故に差別されるということがある。

examples.english: I think, therefore I am. -Descartes
examples.japanese: 「我思う、故に我あり。」ーデカルト

examples.english: People will certainly make mistakes; therefore, we need to think of countermeasures based on that assumption.
examples.japanese: 人はきっとミスをする。故に、それを前提とした対策を考える必要がある。

examples.english: Haiku use a bare minimum of words. Therefore, one has to imagine what is not expressed.
examples.japanese: 俳句は言葉が最小限に抑えられている。それ故に。表現されていないことを想像しなければならない。

points.explanation: 故に・ゆえに A conjunction that presents a reason or a cause.
points.meaning: Because; because of; due to; therefore

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) {Noun(の)/Adjectiveなstem(な)} | 故(に) | |
| 天才(の)故(に) | Become someone is a genius |
| 便利(な) 故(に) | Because something is convenient |
(ii)Sinformal(が) | 故(に) | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun omitted |
| {間違いを/犯す/犯した}(が) 故(に) | Because someone commits/commited an error |
| {美しい/美しかった}(が) 故(に) | Because someone/something is/was beautiful |
| 便利{である/だった/であった}(が) 故(に) | Because something is/was convenient |
| 天才{である/だった/であった}(が) 故(に) | Because someone is/was a genius |
(iii) Sentence1(それ(が)/その) | 故に、Sentence2。 | |
| この議論は前提がおかしい。(それ(が)/その) 故に、結論も間違っている | This argument is based on a wrong premise. Therefore, the conclusion is also wrong |

examples.english: Technological advancements are bound to bring about changes to social environments.
examples.japanese: 技術の発達は社会環境の変化をもたらさずにはおかない。

examples.english: The spread of computers and the expansion of Internet use are bound to promote big changes in education.
examples.japanese: コンピュータの普及とインターネット利用の拡大は大きな教育の変革を促さずにはおかない。

examples.english: This movie is bound to move viewers. (literally: This movie does not leave viewers without moving them.)
examples.japanese: この映画は観る者に感動を与えずにはおかない。

examples.english: Without fail, this novel makes us think about what it is to be human.
examples.japanese: この小説は我々に人間とは何かを考えさせずにはおかない。

examples.english: This accident will undoubtedly affect the relationship between Japan and America.
examples.japanese: この事故は日本とアメリカの関係に影響を及ぼさずにはおかないだろう。

examples.english: She has a musicality that unfailingly captivates her audiences and the superb technique to express it.
examples.japanese: 彼女は聴く者を魅了せずにはおかない音楽性とそれを表現する卓越した技術を持っている。

examples.english: Structures that animals construct according to their environment and needs exhibit in every aspect their wisdom and ideas, and are bound to arouse our curiosity.
examples.japanese: 環境や用途に合わせて動物たちがつくりあげる構造物は、彼らの知恵と工夫がいたるところに見られ、我々の好奇心を惹起せずにはおかない。

points.explanation: A phrase that expresses the idea that someone/something necessarily or naturally causes something to happen.
points.meaning: Be bound to; definitely; unmistakably; unquestionably; undoubtedly; without fail; without doubt

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
Vnegative | ずにはおかない | Exception: する→せずにはおかない |
| 働かさずにはおかない | Someone definitely moves something |

examples.english: You cannot talk about the South American continent without some knowledge of the Inca Empire.
examples.japanese: インカ帝国を知らずして南米大陸を語ることはできない。

examples.english: Our team won the championship before (literally: without waiting for) the ﬁnal game on the ﬁnal day.
examples.japanese: 我々のチームは最終日の最終戦を待たずして優勝が決定した。

examples.english: You should not call others to account when you have not performed your own duties.
examples.japanese: 自分の義務を果たさずして人の責任を問うべきではない。

examples.english: Fumio won the lottery, receiving a large sum of money with no effort.
examples.japanese: 文雄は宝くじが当たって労せずして大金を得た。

examples.english: In the election for a new chairman, unexpectedly (literally: without expecting), everybody agreed (on who it should be).
examples.japanese: 新しい議長の選出で期せずしてみんなの意見が一致した。

examples.english: If we/you don't study now, when will you study?
examples.japanese: 今勉強せずしていつするのか？

examples.english: Mr. Araki died before (literally: without) seeing the completion of the building he'd designed.
examples.japanese: 荒木氏は自分の設計した建物の完成を見ずして亡くなってしまった。

examples.english: I became an offender without meaning to after sending a virus-infected e-mail to individuals and groups outside my company.
examples.japanese: ウイルスに感染した電子メールを社外の個人、団体に送信してしまい、意図せずして加害者になってしまった。

examples.english: You cannot ﬁght without knowing your enemy.
examples.japanese: 敵を知らずしては戦えない。

points.explanation: A phrase meaning "without doing something".
points.meaning: Without ~ing; before (~ing); with no ~; if ~ do not; when ~ do not

points.structure:

| 待たずして | Without waiting |

examples.english: It is cool this summer, so it looks like we can get by without using the air-conditioner.
examples.japanese: 今年の夏は涼しいので、エアコンを使わずとも過ごせそうだ。

examples.english: Because I have several close friends in Chicago, I don't have to stay at a hotel.
examples.japanese: シカゴには親しい友人が何人かいるので、ホテルに泊まらずともよい。

examples.english: If you can go to Europe this cheaply, even if you don't especially like to travel, you'll probably want to go.
examples.japanese: こんなに安くヨーロッパへ行けるのなら、旅行好きならずとも行ってみたいと思うだろう。

examples.english: (Even) if we cannot meet up in Tokyo, we will meet in Osaka for sure.
examples.japanese: 東京で会えずとも、大阪では必ず会える。

examples.english: I can guess how much he can do without even giving him a test.
examples.japanese: 彼がどのくらいできるかはテストをせずとも見当がつく。

examples.english: We can repair this sort of trouble here at the store without sending (the product) to the service centre.
examples.japanese: この程度の故障ならサービスセンター送らずともこの店で修理できます。

examples.english: This cell phone can be voice activated, so you can make a call using just your voice, without having to punch any numbers.
examples.japanese: この携帯電話は音声による操作が可能で、数字キーを押さずとも声だけで電話をかけられる。

examples.english: From now on it will be necessary to have a user interface that doesn't require special training.
examples.japanese: これからは特別な訓練を受けずとも使えるようなユーザーインターフェースが必要となるだろう。

examples.english: This theory is hard to understand, so it is all right if you don't understand it right away.
examples.japanese: この理論は難解なので、今すぐ分からずともよい。

examples.english: Many people, even if they were not baseball fans, paid attention to the baseball strike this time because it (was an event that) made them think about what professional sports should be like in the future (literally: from now on).
examples.japanese: 今回の野球ストは、これからのプロスポーツあり方を考えさせる出来事として、野球ファンならずとも注目する人が多かった。

points.explanation: A conjunctive phrase that indicates negative concession: "even if ~ not".
points.meaning: Without ~ing; even if ~ not; if ~ not

provenance.sourceLabel: DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集)

points.structure:
(i) Vnegative | ずとも | Exception: する→せずとも |
| 使わずとも | Even if one doesn’t use something; without using something |
(ii) Nounなら | ずとも | |
| 専門家ならずとも | Even if someone is not a specialist |
